Five questions to ask of any "X did it"

  1. Who is saying it? A court, a government, one minister, a company with something to sell, or the attackers themselves.
  2. Was anyone caught? A person in custody can be questioned and tried. A group name on Telegram cannot.
  3. Is the evidence public? If not, you are being asked to trust the speaker.
  4. Does anyone with access disagree? A prosecutor who will not confirm, an ally with "low confidence", a second ministry that says "too early".
  5. Is it the hand or the sender? Convicting the man who lit the fire is not the same as proving who paid him.

NL – Vijf vragen bij elke "X deed het": Wie zegt het? Is er iemand gevat? Is het bewijs publiek? Spreekt iemand met toegang het tegen? Gaat het over de hand of over de opdrachtgever?

What it shows: Europe is good at catching the people who light the fires and poor at proving, in public, who sent them. For hacks it is weaker still: in two years not one foreign hacker stood before a European judge in the cases in this file. The honest summary is not "Russia is behind everything" and not "nothing is proven". It is that the proof is solid for sabotage and spying by hired hands, official but unchecked for the big hacks, and absent for most drone alarms.NL – Wat het toont: Europa is goed in het vatten van wie de branden aansteekt en zwak in het publiek bewijzen wie hen stuurde. Voor hacks is het nog zwakker: in twee jaar stond in de gevallen van dit dossier geen enkele buitenlandse hacker voor een Europese rechter. De eerlijke samenvatting is niet "Rusland zit overal achter" en ook niet "niets is bewezen". Het bewijs is stevig voor sabotage en spionage door handlangers, officieel maar oncontroleerbaar voor de grote hacks, en afwezig voor de meeste dronealarmen.

Limits of this tracker

  • It covers the cases worked out in this file, not every incident in the register. Most of the 236 register incidents have nobody named and are not repeated here.
  • The level is my reading of public reporting found by search up to 15 November 2026. Where reports differ, the lower level is used.
  • A level says how firmly someone is named, not whether they did it. L0 does not mean innocent; L4 does not mean proven.
  • For the pages added on 13–15 November the linked sources were not opened one by one; see the Sources page.

The earlier list: formal attributions of hacks, by state

Russia · Rusland

  • Poland's energy sites, 29 Dec 2025: attributed by the EU and UK to Russia's FSB security service (Centre 16); sanctions on 13 Jul 2026.
  • Germany's air traffic control (2024 attack): attributed by Germany to military intelligence (APT28) on 12 Dec 2025.
  • Denmark's water utility and election-period attacks: attributed by Danish military intelligence on 18 Dec 2025 to two pro-Russian groups linked to the Russian state.
  • Norway's dam, 7 Apr 2025: attributed by Norway's security service to pro-Russian hackers in Aug 2025.
  • Sweden: a heating plant targeted by a group linked to Russian intelligence (spring 2025).
  • Czechia: military-intelligence hackers took over internet routers (2026).
  • The group NoName057(16) knocked websites offline in Belgium, Italy, Czechia, Estonia and others; a European police operation hit it in July 2025.

The most often named state. Of the state-linked spying groups the EU cyber agency tracked, 47.6% were linked to Russia.

Iran · Iran

  • French freezer sabotage, 11–12 Oct 2026: attributed by France on 9 Nov 2026 to Shahid Kaveh, a unit of the Revolutionary Guards.
  • A Polish nuclear research centre said early signs of a blocked attack pointed to Iran (Mar 2026); not confirmed.

One formal attribution in Europe in these two years. US agencies reportedly hold only low confidence in it, and Iran denies it. The Belgian wave is not attributed.

China · China

  • Czechia's Foreign Ministry: attributed by the Czech government to APT31 (a hacking group linked to the Chinese state) on 28 May 2025.
  • Norway: the security service said Salt Typhoon exploited network devices (Feb 2026).
  • A wider espionage campaign reached sensitive systems in more than 37 countries (reported Feb 2026).

Named for espionage, not sabotage. Norway's security service says China dominates its cyber threat picture.

North Korea · Noord-Korea

  • Binance, 29 Oct 2026: about $6.3 billion stolen, attributed to a North Korea-linked group; about $3 billion frozen within days.

Named for theft of money. Of the state-linked spying groups the EU cyber agency tracked, 14.1% were linked to North Korea.

Criminal groups · Criminele groepen

  • Ransomware groups named by victims or authorities include Qilin, Akira, SafePay, Rhysida, LockBit and TheGentlemen.
  • Many attacks on towns, hospitals and companies in this file are for ransom, not politics.

The largest group by number of victims. The EU cyber agency calls financially motivated attacks the greatest short-term threat.

Not attributed · Niet toegewezen

  • The Belgian freezer wave of 1–2 Nov 2026.
  • Denmark's population register, Romania's land registry, Liechtenstein's owners register, Latvia's vehicle register.
  • Lithuania's registers: prosecutors suspect a foreign state but have named none.

For most incidents nobody is named. An attacker's own claim is not an attribution.

Europe · Europa
In plain words · In gewone woorden

The biggest outages of online services since 2025, what caused each one, and who is blamed when it was an attack. Almost half were cyberattacks; the rest were the companies' own faults, power failures, or have no published cause.

NL: De grootste storingen van onlinediensten sinds 2025, wat elke veroorzaakte, en wie de schuld krijgt bij een aanval. Bijna de helft waren cyberaanvallen; de rest waren eigen fouten van de bedrijven, stroomproblemen, of heeft geen bekendgemaakte oorzaak.

Global outages: when the world's biggest services went down

1 January 2025 to 19 November 2026, plus background from 2024: 54 outages of major online services and company systems. 22 were cyberattacks; 22 were technical faults or changes at the companies themselves, 4 were power or cooling failures, and for 6 no cause has been published.

NL: 1 januari 2025 tot 19 november 2026, plus achtergrond uit 2024: 54 storingen bij grote onlinediensten en bedrijfssystemen. 22 waren cyberaanvallen; 22 waren technische fouten of wijzigingen bij de bedrijven zelf, 4 waren stroom- of koelingsproblemen, en voor 6 is geen oorzaak bekendgemaakt.

In plain words

An outage here means a big online service, network or company system that stopped working for many people at once. Each card shows two separate things: the cause, which is what happened, and for cyberattacks also who is blamed, which can be only a claim. The labels say how firm a statement is: Confirmed means the company or an authority said so, Reported means credible media said so, Claimed means only the attackers or an unverified party said so, Suspected means it is a guess, and Not published means no explanation has been given yet. The descriptions are in English, each with a Dutch summary.

NL: Een storing betekent hier dat een grote onlinedienst, een netwerk of een bedrijfssysteem uitviel voor veel mensen tegelijk. Elke kaart toont twee aparte dingen: de oorzaak, dus wat er gebeurde, en bij cyberaanvallen ook wie de schuld krijgt, wat soms alleen een bewering is. De labels tonen hoe stevig een uitspraak is: Bevestigd betekent dat het bedrijf of een overheid het zei, Gemeld dat betrouwbare media het zeiden, Geclaimd dat alleen de aanvallers of een niet-geverifieerde partij het zeiden, Vermoed dat het een gok is, en Niet gepubliceerd dat er nog geen uitleg is. De beschrijvingen zijn in het Engels, elk met een Nederlandse samenvatting.

Scope: unlike the rest of this file, which is about Europe, this page is worldwide by design: it lists big companies and services anywhere in the world, not only in Europe.

NL: In tegenstelling tot de rest van dit dossier, dat over Europa gaat, is deze pagina bewust wereldwijd: ze toont grote bedrijven en diensten overal ter wereld, niet alleen in Europa.

The outages, newest first

54 of 54 shown

18 Nov 2026SonyPSN gaming and social services, sign-in and game launchCause not publishedNot published

What happened

Sony's status page said players might have difficulty launching games, apps or network features. Reports on Downdetector peaked at more than 8,000 for the US, according to GV Wire. It came around the launch of the game GTA 6. Some outlets describe a second disruption on 19 November (Sportskeeda, Digit). We could not confirm it from a primary source or a major outlet, so it is not counted. We did not confirm that the 18 November official statement covered this event.

NL: Op de statuspagina van Sony stond dat spelers mogelijk problemen hadden met het starten van games, apps of netwerkfuncties. Volgens GV Wire liepen de meldingen op Downdetector op tot meer dan 8.000 in de VS. Het gebeurde rond de lancering van de game GTA 6. Enkele media spreken van een tweede storing op 19 november; dat kon niet bij een primaire bron of groot medium worden bevestigd. Of de verklaring van 18 november deze storing dekte, is niet bevestigd.

Company: Sony (PlayStation Network). Service: PSN gaming and social services, sign-in and game launch

Duration: About 40 minutes per Sony's status page (1:58 p.m. to about 2:37 p.m. ET); user reports continued; TechRepublic reports two outages around the GTA 6 launch. Where: Global (reports centred on the US)

What caused it

No cause published. Sony's status page named no cause. Commentators suggest launch-day traffic; no source confirms it. Not published

NL: Geen oorzaak bekendgemaakt. Sony noemde op de statuspagina geen oorzaak. Commentatoren wijzen op drukte rond de lancering; geen enkele bron bevestigt dat.

17 Nov 2026US National Security AgencyNSANet, the NSA's classified internal communications networkTechnical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

CNN first reported the classified network was down; the Wall Street Journal reported it was linked to a software update. Reports say the outage slowed analysts' work and forced staff to change when they came to the Fort Meade campus. The NSA itself described only 'temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance' (per press). On 18 November DNI Jay Clayton said the disruption followed a patch for PHP vulnerabilities after which some systems did not restart as expected, and that there was no evidence of a cyberattack.

NL: CNN meldde als eerste dat het geclassificeerde netwerk uitviel; de Wall Street Journal meldde een verband met een software-update. De NSA zelf sprak volgens de pers alleen van 'tijdelijke degradatie tijdens gepland routineonderhoud'. Op 18 november zei nationale inlichtingendirecteur Jay Clayton dat de storing volgde op een patch voor PHP-kwetsbaarheden waarna sommige systemen niet zoals verwacht herstartten, en dat er geen bewijs is voor een cyberaanval.

Duration: Not stated; restoration not confirmed as of 18 Nov per press. Where: US (Fort Meade, Maryland)

What caused it

DNI Jay Clayton linked the outage to a patch for PHP vulnerabilities after which some systems failed to restart as expected, with no evidence of a cyberattack (as reported by The Record; the Wall Street Journal's anonymous source said the NSA was updating its software). The NSA called it scheduled routine maintenance. Confirmed

NL: Nationale inlichtingendirecteur Jay Clayton bracht de storing in verband met een patch voor PHP-kwetsbaarheden waarna sommige systemen niet zoals verwacht herstartten, zonder bewijs voor een cyberaanval (volgens The Record; de anonieme bron van de Wall Street Journal sprak van een software-update). De NSA sprak van gepland routineonderhoud.

16 Nov 2026JPMorgan ChaseChase online and mobile banking, some branches; payments to and…Technical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

Customers reported trouble logging in and an in-app message 'Some services aren't available'; Downdetector counted more than 4,700 Chase reports by 2 p.m. ET, according to press. Other banks (reports named Bank of America, Wells Fargo, US Bank) were listed by users; Chase said they were affected only where they transacted with Chase. Early Warning Services said the Zelle network itself was not down. Bank of America reportedly said its systems were operating normally. On 18 November DNI Jay Clayton and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was no indication of a cyberattack behind the recent outages (the DNI's remarks cited banking outages in general).

NL: Klanten meldden problemen met inloggen en een bericht in de app 'Some services aren't available'; volgens de pers telde Downdetector tegen 14.00 uur ET meer dan 4.700 meldingen over Chase. Gebruikers noemden ook andere banken (Bank of America, Wells Fargo, US Bank); Chase zegt dat die alleen hinder hadden voor zover ze transacties met Chase deden. Early Warning Services zegt dat het Zelle-netwerk zelf niet uitviel. Bank of America zou hebben gezegd dat de systemen normaal werkten. Op 18 november zeiden nationale inlichtingendirecteur Jay Clayton en minister Marco Rubio dat er geen aanwijzing is voor een cyberaanval achter de recente storingen (de DNI sprak ook over storingen bij banken in het algemeen).

Service: Chase online and mobile banking, some branches; payments to and from Chase (incl. Zelle transfers)

Duration: Several hours on Monday 16 Nov; Chase said around 6:30 p.m. ET that transactions were posting normally. Where: US

What caused it

Chase said it was a temporary issue caused by a software bug in an on-premises hardware system and was not cyber-related; it said 'this is not a systemic issue'. A source told CNN an update on the bank's own computer systems inadvertently caused the problems, not a cloud issue or an attack. Not shown to be linked to the Microsoft or FAA incidents. Confirmed

NL: Chase zegt dat het ging om een tijdelijk probleem door een softwarefout in een on-premises hardwaresysteem en dat het niet met cyber te maken had; 'dit is geen systemisch probleem'. Een bron zei tegen CNN dat een update op de eigen computersystemen van de bank de problemen onbedoeld veroorzaakte, geen cloudprobleem of aanval. 13 Nov 2026FAANationwide ground stop; air traffic control telecommunications networkTechnical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

The FAA halted all departing flights nationwide on Friday 13 November after a communications problem. The FAA says radar feeds and aircraft communications were disrupted at 17 of 22 en-route control centres. The FAA said about 12,462 flights were cancelled, including 9,082 by major airlines, but that not all cancellations were directly caused by the ground stop; all flights landed safely. On 17-18 November the FAA paused further Juniper router installations. On 18 November DNI Jay Clayton and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was no indication of a cyberattack behind the recent outages and that the incidents were separate.

NL: Op vrijdag 13 november legde de FAA alle vertrekkende vluchten in de VS stil na een communicatieprobleem. Volgens de FAA vielen radarbeelden en communicatie met vliegtuigen uit bij 17 van de 22 verkeersleidingscentra. De FAA zegt dat ongeveer 12.462 vluchten werden geschrapt, waaronder 9.082 door grote maatschappijen, maar dat niet alle annuleringen rechtstreeks door de grondstop kwamen; alle vluchten landden veilig. Op 17-18 november stopte de FAA de verdere installatie van Juniper-routers. Op 18 november zeiden nationale inlichtingendirecteur Jay Clayton en minister van Buitenlandse Zaken Marco Rubio dat er geen aanwijzing is voor een cyberaanval achter de recente storingen en dat het om afzonderlijke incidenten ging.

Company: FAA (US Federal Aviation Administration). Service: Nationwide ground stop; air traffic control telecommunications network

Duration: About 4.5 hours: problem from about 3:30 p.m. ET, ground stop lifted around 8:15 p.m. ET (Washington Post, as summarised by press); delays lingered after. Where: US (all departures halted nationwide); some Europe-US flights were also delayed or cancelled according to press reports

What caused it

The FAA said a flood of data on its telecommunications network (about 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds) destabilised legacy equipment. It named a radio site at El Dorado, Arkansas, where contractor L3Harris was installing a new Juniper router, and a radar site at Amarillo, Texas. The FAA disabled the functionality on the originating Juniper routers and on more than 60 others as a precaution. The root cause is still under investigation; HPE, maker of Juniper, says the devices worked as intended ('They did not fail', per press). The FAA said it had no indication of a cyberattack (per press reports of its statement). Defective equipment versus installation/configuration error is not established. Confirmed

NL: De FAA zegt dat een stortvloed aan data op haar telecommunicatienetwerk (ongeveer 1.000 verbindingspogingen per 4 tot 5 seconden) oude apparatuur ontregelde. Ze noemt een radiosite in El Dorado (Arkansas), waar aannemer L3Harris een nieuwe Juniper-router installeerde, en een radarsite in Amarillo (Texas). De FAA schakelde de functie uit op de router van oorsprong en voorzorgshalve op meer dan 60 andere. De grondoorzaak wordt nog onderzocht; HPE, producent van Juniper, zegt dat de apparaten werkten zoals bedoeld. De FAA zegt geen aanwijzing te hebben voor een cyberaanval. Defecte apparatuur of een installatie- of configuratiefout is niet vastgesteld.

12–13 Nov 2026MicrosoftExchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot, SharePointTechnical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

Exchange Online and Outlook were the worst hit; Teams, Copilot and SharePoint were also disrupted.

NL: Exchange Online en Outlook waren het zwaarst getroffen; ook Teams, Copilot en SharePoint hadden hinder.

Duration: About 24 hours (16:20 UTC 12 Nov to 16:10 UTC 13 Nov); sources differ on exact start. Where: Global

What caused it

Microsoft's preliminary report, as relayed by media, points to a latent defect from a July 2026 fix applied to Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers (the servers that act as the entry point for Microsoft 365 network traffic). These became overwhelmed under load after Teams traffic failed over to the gateway shared with Exchange Online. About 14% of that gateway's capacity was also out of service for an unrelated reason. Microsoft said it saw no evidence of malicious activity. The final report was not yet seen. Confirmed

NL: Het voorlopige rapport van Microsoft, zoals door media weergegeven, wijst op een sluimerende fout door een correctie van juli 2026 op netwerkgateways van Microsoft 365 (de servers waarlangs het netwerkverkeer van Microsoft 365 binnenkomt). Die raakten onder belasting overbelast nadat Teams-verkeer was overgeschakeld naar de gateway die ook Exchange Online gebruikt. Ongeveer 14% van de capaciteit van die gateway lag bovendien stil om een andere reden. Microsoft zei geen aanwijzingen voor kwaadwillige activiteit te hebben gezien. Het eindrapport werd nog niet gezien.

Sources

What happened

Several Google Cloud services in the London region were disrupted; outlets reported knock-on effects at UK banks and apps (including Revolut, Lloyds and HSBC), courts and a parcel firm.

Duration: Several hours: began 06:08 UTC; mitigation about 11:36 UTC per one source, most workloads recovered about 14:48 London time per Computer Weekly (sources differ). Where: UK (London region)

What caused it

Other outlets claim generators failed to engage or that other zones did not absorb the load; these claims are not confirmed by Google. Confirmed

Andere media beweren dat generatoren niet inschakelden of dat andere zones de belasting niet opvingen; Google heeft dat niet bevestigd.

12 Oct 2026Ahold Delhaizewebsites, apps and online ordering; Albert Heijn deliveries and…CyberattackConfirmed

What happened

Ahold Delhaize said on 12 October 2026 that it had a 'security issue' in its network and was taking some systems offline; stores stayed open. Websites, apps and online ordering of several brands were disrupted, and Albert Heijn's website, app and home delivery went down. Etos, Gall & Gall, Delhaize (Belgium) and US chains were also affected. Reuters (via Teiss) reported that Albert Heijn's website returned on 19 October but online deliveries would not resume before Thursday at the earliest; AP reported the US supermarkets back online by 22 October. Retail experts estimated Albert Heijn's missed sales at EUR 120 to 150 million (an outside estimate; the company disclosed no figure).

NL: Ahold Delhaize zei op 12 oktober 2026 dat het een 'beveiligingsprobleem' in zijn netwerk had en bepaalde systemen offline haalde; de winkels bleven open. Websites, apps en online bestellingen van meerdere merken waren verstoord en de website, de app en de thuislevering van Albert Heijn vielen uit. Ook Etos, Gall & Gall, Delhaize (België) en de Amerikaanse ketens werden getroffen. Volgens Reuters (via Teiss) was de website van Albert Heijn op 19 oktober terug, maar zouden online leveringen ten vroegste donderdag hervat worden; volgens AP waren de Amerikaanse supermarkten op 22 oktober weer online. Retailexperts raamden de gemiste omzet van Albert Heijn op 120 tot 150 miljoen euro (een externe schatting; het bedrijf maakte geen cijfer bekend).

Company: Ahold Delhaize (Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Etos, Gall & Gall, Stop & Shop, Food Lion, Hannaford). Service: websites, apps and online ordering; Albert Heijn deliveries and restocking

Duration: about ten days: Albert Heijn website back 19 Oct, deliveries not before 22 Oct; US sites still offline on 19 Oct and reported back online by 22 Oct. Where: Netherlands, Belgium, other Europe, US

What caused it

Ahold Delhaize described a 'security issue' and said it found no evidence that sensitive customer, employee or partner data was stolen. Reuters (via Teiss) reported it informed Dutch police on 19 October. The company has not said whether attackers encrypted files or which kind of attack it was. Sources differ on the start (some say 11 October). Confirmed

NL: Ahold Delhaize sprak van een 'beveiligingsprobleem' en zei geen aanwijzingen te hebben dat gevoelige gegevens van klanten, personeel of partners werden gestolen. Volgens Reuters (via Teiss) verwittigde het op 19 oktober de Nederlandse politie. Het bedrijf zei niet of de aanvallers bestanden versleutelden en om welk soort aanval het ging. Bronnen verschillen over het begin (sommige zeggen 11 oktober).

Who is blamed

Nobody named. In the sources seen no group has claimed it and no authority has named anyone. Nobody named

Europe and Belgium

Directly: Albert Heijn, Etos and Gall & Gall (Netherlands) and Delhaize (Belgium, e-commerce affected).

11-12 Oct 2026 (later wave early Nov 2026)Carrefour, Monoprix and other French supermarket chainsrefrigeration and freezer control systems in hundreds of supermarketsCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

Overnight on 11-12 October 2026 attackers hijacked refrigeration controllers in French supermarkets, pushing freezers into defrost at up to 50°C, spoiling food and, according to media, sparking fires. Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets were hit and Monoprix said about 5% of its stores; media estimates of the total range from about 400 to about 700 sites. A broadcaster reported EUR 270,000 of losses at two Alsace stores (not independently confirmed). A second wave on 1-2 November hit supermarkets and food businesses in at least nine European countries (Cybersecurity Dive); Kesko confirmed temperature irregularities at a few stores and Musgrave said 13 SuperValu stores in Ireland were affected.

NL: In de nacht van 11 op 12 oktober 2026 kaapten aanvallers de koelingsbesturing in Franse supermarkten, waardoor diepvriezers tot 50 °C ontdooiden, voedsel verloren ging en er volgens media branden ontstonden. Carrefour zei dat 80 van zijn supermarkten werden getroffen en Monoprix ongeveer 5 procent van zijn winkels; schattingen in de media voor het totaal lopen uiteen van ongeveer 400 tot ongeveer 700 vestigingen. Een omroep meldde 270.000 euro verlies bij twee winkels in de Elzas (niet onafhankelijk bevestigd). Een tweede golf op 1-2 november trof supermarkten en voedingsbedrijven in minstens negen Europese landen (Cybersecurity Dive); Kesko bevestigde temperatuurafwijkingen in enkele winkels en Musgrave zei dat 13 SuperValu-winkels in Ierland getroffen waren.

Company: Carrefour, Monoprix and other French supermarket chains (about 700 commercial sites per France's attribution; second wave across Europe). Service: refrigeration and freezer control systems in hundreds of supermarkets

Duration: overnight attack; stores discarded food; second wave on 1-2 November. Where: France; second wave Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Portugal, Sweden

What caused it

Retailers confirmed a cyberattack on refrigeration controllers. France's cybersecurity agency ANSSI tied the affected systems to Danfoss controllers and said controllers from two other makers were also targeted (as reported); Danfoss said a limited number of systems were affected. Many affected units were reportedly end-of-life or ran outdated software. This was sabotage, not ransomware. Confirmed

NL: De winkelketens bevestigden een cyberaanval op koelingsbesturingen. Het Franse cyberveiligheidsagentschap ANSSI koppelde de getroffen systemen aan besturingen van Danfoss en zei dat ook besturingen van twee andere fabrikanten waren geviseerd (zoals gemeld); Danfoss zei dat een beperkt aantal systemen was getroffen. Veel getroffen toestellen waren naar verluidt verouderd of draaiden verouderde software. Het ging om sabotage, niet om ransomware.

Who is blamed

France says Shahid Kaveh, a unit of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, was behind the October attacks (formal attribution by foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot on 9 November 2026); Paris prosecutors opened a judicial investigation and requested international arrest warrants, France summoned Iran's ambassador and will propose EU sanctions. The technical evidence has not been published and Iran denies it ('baseless and malicious'). US agencies reportedly hold only low confidence in the link (reported by TechCrunch, citing three US officials who spoke to the New York Times). Pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest claimed the attacks on Telegram and then deleted the posts (claims); the Kremlin called Russian involvement absurd. For Belgium (1-2 November), Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said Iran was 'very probably' behind it, citing indications from the security services; Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot said the information is insufficient to hold Iran officially responsible, and the federal prosecutor declined to comment. Formal attribution, contested

Europe and Belgium

France directly; second wave included Belgium and the Netherlands (which chains was not verified; ICA's confirmation of an attack is reported inconsistently and no confirmation was found for Selver).

25 Aug 2026Boston Scientificmanufacturing, order processing and shipping of medical devicesCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

Boston Scientific disclosed in an SEC filing of 26 August 2026 that it had identified on 25 August a cybersecurity incident affecting certain IT systems that caused a global disruption to its operations, including its ability to process and ship customer orders. A filing of 7 September said sterilisation facilities were operating and manufacturing had resumed at most facilities, with no timeline set for full recovery, and flagged possible effects on its third-quarter and full-year 2026 guidance.

NL: Boston Scientific meldde in een beursdocument van 26 augustus 2026 dat het op 25 augustus een cyberincident had vastgesteld dat bepaalde IT-systemen trof en een wereldwijde verstoring van de werking veroorzaakte, waaronder het verwerken en verzenden van bestellingen. Een document van 7 september zei dat de sterilisatie-installaties draaiden en dat de productie in de meeste vestigingen was hervat, zonder tijdschema voor volledig herstel, en wees op mogelijke gevolgen voor de vooruitzichten voor het derde kwartaal en heel 2026.

Duration: not fully recovered as of the 7 September filing; manufacturing resumed at most facilities. Where: Global

What caused it

Boston Scientific called it a cybersecurity incident and was investigating with outside experts. It has not said whether ransomware was involved; one press report says the unauthorised activity was confined to limited on-premises systems. Confirmed

NL: Boston Scientific noemde het een cyberincident en onderzocht het met externe experts. Het zei niet of ransomware in het spel was; volgens een persbericht bleef de onbevoegde activiteit beperkt tot enkele systemen op eigen servers.

Who is blamed

Nobody named; no group has publicly claimed it in the sources seen. Nobody named

Europe and Belgium

No verified effect on a European site (a report that the Cork plant sent staff home could not be confirmed).

16 Jul 2026 (disclosed)Fairlifemilk and dairy production at four US plantsCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

Coca-Cola told the SEC on 16 July 2026 that unauthorised access by a third party to part of Fairlife's systems, including production-related systems, in connection with a ransomware event led to a temporary suspension of Fairlife's US production. On 27 July Coca-Cola said Fairlife had resumed most production across its four US plants and that product quality and safety were unaffected.

NL: Coca-Cola meldde op 16 juli 2026 aan de Amerikaanse beurswaakhond dat onbevoegde toegang door een derde tot een deel van de systemen van Fairlife, inclusief productiegerelateerde systemen, in verband met een ransomware-incident leidde tot een tijdelijke opschorting van de Amerikaanse productie van Fairlife. Op 27 juli zei Coca-Cola dat Fairlife het grootste deel van de productie in zijn vier Amerikaanse fabrieken had hervat en dat de productkwaliteit en -veiligheid niet waren aangetast.

Company: Fairlife (The Coca-Cola Company). Service: milk and dairy production at four US plants

Duration: about 11 days until most production resumed (16 to 27 July, per Coca-Cola statements). Where: US

Asahi first reported a 'systems failure' and then confirmed it was a ransomware attack, with possible personal data exposure. Factories themselves were reportedly not infected; production stopped because order and shipping systems were shut down (reported). Confirmed

NL: Asahi meldde eerst een 'systeemstoring' en bevestigde daarna dat het om een ransomware-aanval ging, met mogelijke blootstelling van persoonsgegevens. De fabrieken zelf waren volgens berichten niet besmet; de productie stopte omdat bestel- en verzendsystemen werden afgesloten (gemeld).

Who is blamed

The Qilin ransomware group listed Asahi on its leak site on 7 October and claimed about 27 GB of stolen data (claim by the group; Bloomberg said it could not verify it). Asahi has not confirmed that Qilin was behind the attack. Claimed

Sources

  • The Star (Bloomberg) — Ransomware gang Qilin claims hack that crippled beermaker Asahi (8 Oct 2025)
  • Computer Weekly — Qilin gang claims cyber attack on Japanese brewing giant (Oct 2025)
  • Just Drinks — Asahi plants resume operations in wake of cyberattack (Oct 2025)
  • Inside.beer — Japan: Asahi needs at least two more months to restore logistics (Nov 2025)
19 Sep 2025Collins Aerospaceshared check-in and boarding software (MUSE) at Heathrow,…CyberattackConfirmed

What happened

A ransomware attack on Collins Aerospace's MUSE software forced airline staff at several European airports to check passengers in manually from 19 September 2025. Collins said the disruption was limited to electronic check-in and baggage drop. AP reported Brussels cancelled about half its flights on the Monday. No cost figure was published in the sources seen.

NL: Een ransomware-aanval op de MUSE-software van Collins Aerospace dwong het personeel van luchtvaartmaatschappijen op meerdere Europese luchthavens vanaf 19 september 2025 om passagiers handmatig in te checken. Collins zei dat de verstoring beperkt bleef tot elektronische check-in en bagage-afgifte. Volgens AP schrapte Brussel op maandag ongeveer de helft van zijn vluchten. In de geraadpleegde bronnen werd geen kostenraming gepubliceerd.

Company: Collins Aerospace (RTX) - check-in system at European airports. Service: shared check-in and boarding software (MUSE) at Heathrow, Brussels, Berlin and Dublin

Duration: a few days at the worst-hit airports (Brussels still had 6% of flights cancelled on Wednesday 24 September, per 7sur7); exact end not verified. Where: UK, Belgium, Germany, Ireland

What caused it

ENISA (the EU cybersecurity agency) said the disruption was caused by a third-party ransomware incident, and Collins' parent RTX said in an SEC Form 8-K that ransomware affected systems supporting MUSE (as reported by media; filing not opened). Confirmed

NL: ENISA (het EU-agentschap voor cyberveiligheid) zei dat de verstoring werd veroorzaakt door een ransomware-incident bij een derde partij, en moederbedrijf RTX meldde in een 8-K-document aan de Amerikaanse beurswaakhond dat ransomware systemen trof die MUSE ondersteunen (zoals gemeld door media; het document zelf werd niet geopend).

Who is blamed

Nobody has been named. The UK National Crime Agency arrested a man in his 40s in West Sussex on suspicion of Computer Misuse Act offences; he was released on conditional bail and no charge was found in the sources seen. No ransomware group has claimed the attack; media quoted unnamed security experts linking it to the HardBit variant, which is not an official finding. Nobody named

Europe and Belgium

Directly hit: Brussels Airport (Belgium), Heathrow, Berlin Brandenburg and Dublin.

Also in this file: the transport page for 30 countries.

Sources

18 Sep 2025OptusEmergency calls (Triple Zero) on the Optus networkTechnical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

Calls to Triple Zero (000) failed for Optus customers in several Australian states during a firewall upgrade. Reports give roughly 600 calls affected, and the outage was linked to deaths; the count varies by source (three initially, later reports say two to four).

NL: Oproepen naar het Australische noodnummer Triple Zero (000) mislukten voor Optus-klanten in meerdere staten tijdens een firewall-upgrade. Volgens de berichtgeving waren er ongeveer 600 oproepen getroffen en werd de storing in verband gebracht met overlijdens; het aantal verschilt per bron (eerst drie, later twee tot vier).

Company: Optus (Singtel). Service: Emergency calls (Triple Zero) on the Optus network

Duration: Unknown (not stated in the sources found). Where: South Australia, Western Australia, Northern Territory, parts of NSW

What caused it

Optus said the fault arose during a planned firewall upgrade; its CEO said an employee did not follow protocols. A later report cited by The Register found at least ten mistakes in the upgrade. Confirmed

NL: Optus zei dat de fout optrad tijdens een geplande firewall-upgrade; de CEO zei dat een medewerker de procedures niet volgde. Een later rapport waarover The Register bericht, vond minstens tien fouten in de upgrade.

Sources

  • The Register — Ten mistakes marred firewall upgrade at Australian telco (2025-12-19)
  • The Register — Firewall upgrade linked to three deaths after Australian telco cut off emergency calls (2025-09-21)
2 Sep 2025Bridgestone Americastyre manufacturing plants in North AmericaCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

A cyberattack announced on 2 September 2025 disrupted Bridgestone Americas manufacturing plants, including two in Aiken County, South Carolina; the mayor of Joliette, Quebec said he believed all North American plants were affected (his belief, not confirmed by the company). Production was reported put on hold at several locations. Bridgestone described the incident as confined, said some plants were affected and were being methodically returned to full operation. No cost figure was found.

NL: Een cyberaanval, bekendgemaakt op 2 september 2025, verstoorde fabrieken van Bridgestone Americas, onder meer twee in Aiken County (South Carolina); de burgemeester van Joliette (Quebec) zei te geloven dat alle Noord-Amerikaanse fabrieken getroffen waren (zijn overtuiging, niet bevestigd door het bedrijf). De productie lag volgens berichten stil op meerdere locaties. Bridgestone noemde het incident beperkt, zei dat sommige fabrieken getroffen waren en stapsgewijs naar volledige werking werden teruggebracht. Er werd geen kostenraming gevonden.

Duration: not verified; production halts at several plants reported as temporary. Where: US, Canada

What caused it

Bridgestone told BleepingComputer it was investigating a confined cyberattack affecting certain manufacturing plants and that no customer data or interfaces were compromised (company statement, as reported). Ransomware was not confirmed. Confirmed

NL: Bridgestone zei tegen BleepingComputer dat het een beperkte cyberaanval onderzocht die bepaalde fabrieken trof en dat geen klantgegevens of -koppelingen werden aangetast (verklaring van het bedrijf, zoals gemeld). Ransomware werd niet bevestigd.

Who is blamed

Nobody named; no group has claimed it in the sources seen. Nobody named

Sources

  • GCN — Bridgestone cyberattack disrupts North American production (Sep 2025)

31 Aug 2025 (production paused from 1 Sep)Jaguar Land Rovercar production, sales and parts systemsCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

JLR shut down its IT systems after a cyber incident and paused vehicle production from 1 September 2025; the pause was extended several times and production restarted in stages from early October (RTE, 9 October). JLR reported exceptional costs of £196 million relating to the cyber incident in the quarter to 30 September 2025 (company figure; its total exceptional items of £238 million also included £42 million of redundancy costs). The independent Cyber Monitoring Centre estimated the cost to the UK economy at about £1.9 billion (central estimate, range £1.6 to 2.1 billion; an estimate, not JLR's bill).

NL: JLR sloot zijn IT-systemen af na een cyberincident en legde de autoproductie vanaf 1 september 2025 stil; de stilstand werd meermaals verlengd en de productie werd vanaf begin oktober in fasen herstart (RTE, 9 oktober). JLR meldde uitzonderlijke kosten van 196 miljoen pond met betrekking tot het cyberincident in het kwartaal tot 30 september 2025 (cijfer van het bedrijf; de totale uitzonderlijke posten van 238 miljoen pond omvatten ook 42 miljoen pond herstructureringskosten). Het onafhankelijke Cyber Monitoring Centre raamde de kost voor de Britse economie op ongeveer 1,9 miljard pond (centrale schatting, bandbreedte 1,6 tot 2,1 miljard pond; een schatting, niet de rekening van JLR).

Duration: production halted about six weeks (Computer Weekly); restarted in stages from early October 2025. Where: UK (Solihull, Halewood, Wolverhampton plants)

What caused it

JLR confirmed a 'cyber incident' and shut systems as a precaution. JLR did not publish the type of attack in the sources seen. A UK government guarantee of about £1.5 billion for the supply chain was reported by media. Confirmed

NL: JLR bevestigde een 'cyberincident' en sloot systemen preventief af. JLR publiceerde in de geraadpleegde bronnen het type aanval niet. Media meldden een Britse overheidsgarantie van ongeveer 1,5 miljard pond voor de toeleveringsketen.

Who is blamed

The group calling itself Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters (a self-described merger of Scattered Spider, Lapsus$ and ShinyHunters) claimed responsibility. Not confirmed by JLR or an authority in the sources seen; no arrests tied to JLR were found. Claimed

Europe and Belgium

UK plants. Effects on Europe's supply chain were reported by media; no specific Belgian effect found.

28 Jul 2025Aeroflotairline IT systems, flight operationsCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

A cyberattack caused a mass outage of Aeroflot's IT systems on 28 July 2025. Russia's prosecutor's office put the cancellations at more than 100 flights; counts differ by source (some reports say 108 of about 260 scheduled flights, others 60 or more). Russian experts quoted by Meduza estimated first-day losses at about 259 million roubles (an estimate, not an Aeroflot figure); another expert estimated total losses of US$10 to 50 million including recovery costs.

NL: Een cyberaanval veroorzaakte op 28 juli 2025 een massale uitval van de IT-systemen van Aeroflot. Het Russische openbaar ministerie sprak van meer dan 100 geschrapte vluchten; de aantallen verschillen per bron (volgens sommige berichten 108 van ongeveer 260 geplande vluchten, volgens andere minstens 60). Russische experts geciteerd door Meduza raamden het verlies op de eerste dag op ongeveer 259 miljoen roebel (een schatting, geen cijfer van Aeroflot); een andere expert raamde het totale verlies op 10 tot 50 miljoen dollar, inclusief herstelkosten.

Duration: one day of major disruption (28 July); further recovery time not verified. Where: Russia

What caused it

Russia's prosecutor's office said a cyberattack caused the mass outage and opened a criminal investigation (authority). The hackers claimed they destroyed about 7,000 servers and workstations; this was not independently verified. Confirmed

NL: Het Russische openbaar ministerie zei dat een cyberaanval de massale uitval veroorzaakte en opende een strafonderzoek (overheid). De hackers beweerden ongeveer 7.000 servers en werkstations te hebben vernietigd; dit werd niet onafhankelijk bevestigd.

Who is blamed

The groups Silent Crow and the Belarusian Cyber Partisans claimed the attack as support for Ukraine (claim by the groups). No authority has named them in the sources seen. Claimed

Sources

  • AP via Click On Detroit — Cyberattack on Russian airline Aeroflot causes the cancellation of more than 100 flights (28 Jul 2025)
  • Security Affairs — Pro-Ukraine hacktivists claim cyberattack on Aeroflot (Jul 2025)
  • Meduza — Assessing Aeroflot's aftermath (30 Jul 2025)
25 Jul 2025Orangemanagement platforms for business customers and some consumer servicesCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

Orange said it detected a cyberattack on one of its information systems on 25 July 2025 and isolated the affected systems; the isolation measures disrupted some management services and platforms for business customers and some consumer services, mainly in France (Orange press release, 28 July). Restoration was reported as expected around 30 July (media). No cost figure was found.

NL: Orange zei op 25 juli 2025 een cyberaanval op een van zijn informatiesystemen te hebben vastgesteld en de getroffen systemen te hebben geïsoleerd; door die isolatie waren sommige beheerdiensten en platformen voor zakelijke klanten en enkele consumentendiensten verstoord, vooral in Frankrijk (persbericht van Orange, 28 juli). Het herstel werd volgens de media rond 30 juli verwacht. Er werd geen kostenraming gevonden.

Company: Orange (France). Service: management platforms for business customers and some consumer services

Duration: about five days (restoration reported as expected around 30 July). Where: France

What caused it

Orange confirmed a cyberattack on one of its information systems and filed a complaint on 28 July. Media report there was no evidence at that stage that customer data was extracted (secondary reporting; Orange declined further comment). Confirmed

NL: Orange bevestigde een cyberaanval op een van zijn informatiesystemen en diende op 28 juli klacht in. Media melden dat er op dat moment geen aanwijzingen waren dat klantgegevens waren buitgemaakt (secundaire berichtgeving; Orange wilde niet verder commentaar geven).

Who is blamed

Nobody named by Orange, and no authority has named anyone. Nobody named

Europe and Belgium

France only. A separate July 2025 data breach at Orange Belgium (reported as affecting 850,000 customers) was a data breach, not an outage; no source linking the two was found.

Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver was unreachable worldwide, so many users could not resolve websites through it.

NL: De DNS-resolver 1.1.1.1 van Cloudflare was wereldwijd onbereikbaar, waardoor veel gebruikers via die dienst geen websites konden opzoeken.

NL: Cloudflare zei dat een interne configuratiefout de oorzaak was, geen aanval of BGP-kaping: een sluimerende misconfiguratie werd geactiveerd toen een wijziging de 1.1.1.1-prefixen introk.

3 Jul 2025Ingram Microordering website, licence provisioning and distribution platforms…CyberattackConfirmed

What happened

Ingram Micro's website and online ordering went down around 3 July 2025; the company later said ransomware had hit internal systems and it shut down systems as a precaution. Press reports say ordering was reactivated region by region from about 9 July. No cost figure was found.

NL: De website en het online bestelsysteem van Ingram Micro vielen rond 3 juli 2025 uit; het bedrijf zei later dat ransomware interne systemen had getroffen en dat het systemen preventief afsloot. Volgens de pers werd bestellen vanaf ongeveer 9 juli regio per regio hersteld. Er werd geen kostenraming gevonden.

Service: ordering website, licence provisioning and distribution platforms (world's largest IT distributor)

What caused it

Ingram Micro said it had identified ransomware on certain internal systems, took some systems offline and notified law enforcement. Sources told BleepingComputer the access may have been through a GlobalProtect VPN; not officially confirmed. Confirmed

NL: Ingram Micro zei ransomware te hebben vastgesteld op bepaalde interne systemen, nam sommige systemen offline en verwittigde de politiediensten. Bronnen vertelden BleepingComputer dat de toegang mogelijk via een GlobalProtect-VPN verliep; niet officieel bevestigd.

BleepingComputer reported that a ransom note found on employee devices claimed to be from the SafePay group (the group's own note, as reported). Ingram Micro has not named an attacker and no authority has. Claimed

Google Cloud API requests returned errors worldwide; Spotify and others were affected and Cloudflare reported knock-on effects on some of its services.

5 Jun 2025United Natural Foodsgrocery wholesale and distribution (main supplier to Whole Foods)CyberattackConfirmed

What happened

UNFI took systems offline after detecting unauthorised activity on 5 June 2025, and its filing said the incident had caused temporary disruptions to order fulfilment. Whole Foods and other grocers reported shortages and empty shelves. UNFI later said it expected the incident to reduce fiscal-2025 net sales by about US$350 to 400 million (company guidance, as reported by Teiss).

UNFI's Form 8-K reports unauthorised activity on its IT systems and containment measures; the 26 June 8-K says the company holds cyber insurance it expects to be adequate. The company did not publicly name the type of attack; observers suspected ransomware (suspected). Confirmed

NL: Het 8-K-document van UNFI meldt onbevoegde activiteit op zijn IT-systemen en beheersmaatregelen; het 8-K van 26 juni zegt dat het bedrijf een cyberverzekering heeft die volgens zijn verwachting volstaat. Nobody named. Nobody named

26 May 2025 (website restored 29 May)Victoria's Secretwebsite and some in-store services (returns of online orders, gift…CyberattackReported

Victoria's Secret shut its corporate systems and e-commerce site on 26 May 2025 as a precaution after a security incident, and restored the website on 29 May (Reuters). Service: website and some in-store services (returns of online orders, gift cards, rewards, credit cards, per press reports)

The company said it took systems offline as a precaution after a 'security incident' and engaged outside experts. It did not say publicly whether it was ransomware; media call it a cyber incident. Reported

late Apr 2025 onwardsCo-op Groupfood stores' stock supply, payments, member systemsCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

After a cyber attack in late April 2025 Co-op stores had empty shelves for weeks. In its half-year report (six months to 5 July 2025) Co-op said the attack cut sales revenue by about £206 million and operating profit by £80 million (£20 million one-off costs and £60 million lost sales). In March 2026 its full-year results estimated the direct impact of the attack at £285 million of revenue and £107 million of profit (£86 million lost margin and £21 million one-off costs); these are Co-op management estimates.

NL: Na een cyberaanval eind april 2025 hadden de Co-op-winkels weken lang lege schappen. In zijn halfjaarverslag (zes maanden tot 5 juli 2025) zei Co-op dat de aanval de omzet met ongeveer 206 miljoen pond en de bedrijfswinst met 80 miljoen pond verminderde (20 miljoen pond eenmalige kosten en 60 miljoen pond gemiste verkoop). In maart 2026 raamden de jaarresultaten de rechtstreekse impact op 285 miljoen pond omzet en 107 miljoen pond winst (86 miljoen pond gemiste marge en 21 miljoen pond eenmalige kosten); dat zijn schattingen van het Co-op-management.

Duration: shelves affected for weeks; recovery details beyond that not verified. Where: UK

What caused it

Co-op confirmed a cyber attack and that the data of all 6.5 million members was stolen. Reports say the attackers deployed DragonForce ransomware. The Financial Times first reported that Co-op had no cyber insurance; Co-op later confirmed it held no dedicated cyber insurance, though it had cover for operational disruption (as reported by Insurance Business and Insurance Insider). Confirmed

NL: Co-op bevestigde een cyberaanval en dat de gegevens van alle 6,5 miljoen leden werden gestolen. Volgens berichten zette de aanvaller DragonForce-ransomware in. De Financial Times meldde als eerste dat Co-op geen cyberverzekering had; Co-op bevestigde later dat het geen specifieke cyberverzekering had, maar wel dekking voor bedrijfsonderbreking (zoals gemeld door Insurance Business en Insurance Insider).

Who is blamed

DragonForce claimed the attack and told the BBC it had stolen data (claim by the criminal group). Researchers link it to Scattered Spider; the NCA arrested four people on 10 July 2025 over the M&S, Co-op and Harrods attacks without naming a group. Not confirmed by Co-op. Claimed

22 Apr 2025 onwardsMarks & Spenceronline shopping, contactless payments and click-and-collect; food…CyberattackConfirmed

What happened

M&S paused online orders in late April 2025 after a cyber attack and some shelves went empty. Reuters reported online orders resumed on 10 June after a 46-day pause; click-and-collect returned much later. M&S itself estimated the incident would cost about £300 million in operating profit, which it hoped to halve through insurance and cost controls.

NL: M&S schorste eind april 2025 de online bestellingen op na een cyberaanval en sommige schappen raakten leeg. Volgens Reuters werden de online bestellingen op 10 juni hervat na een pauze van 46 dagen; 'click-and-collect' kwam pas veel later terug. M&S zelf raamde de kost op ongeveer 300 miljoen pond operationele winst, die het hoopte te halveren via verzekering en kostenbeheersing.

Service: online shopping, contactless payments and click-and-collect; food stock and supply systems

Duration: online orders paused 46 days (from 25 April to 10 June, per Reuters); click-and-collect returned later; full recovery took months. Where: UK

What caused it

M&S confirmed a cyber attack and later confirmed customer data was stolen. Media report that DragonForce ransomware was used and that attackers entered through a third-party contractor (the TCS help-desk arrangement has been examined); the contractor route is reported, not confirmed in the sources seen. Confirmed

NL: M&S bevestigde een cyberaanval en later ook diefstal van klantgegevens. Media melden dat DragonForce-ransomware werd gebruikt en dat de aanvallers via een externe contractant binnenkwamen (de helpdesk-regeling met TCS werd onderzocht); die toegangsroute is gemeld, niet bevestigd in de geraadpleegde bronnen.

Who is blamed

Researchers and media attribute the attack to Scattered Spider working with the DragonForce ransomware service. The UK National Crime Agency (10 July 2025) arrested four people (aged 17 to 20) over the M&S, Co-op and Harrods attacks, but did not name a group or charge them for M&S in the sources seen. Not confirmed by M&S. Reported

Europe and Belgium

UK retailer; the main effects are in the UK.

16 Apr 2025Zoom / GoDaddy RegistryZoom meetings (zoom.us domain)Technical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

The zoom.us domain stopped resolving, so Zoom meetings and website failed worldwide, including calls in progress.

NL: Het domein zoom.us werd onbereikbaar, waardoor Zoom-vergaderingen en de website wereldwijd uitvielen, ook lopende gesprekken.

Duration: About 1 hour 47 minutes (Zoom: 14:25–16:12 ET). Where: Global

What caused it

Zoom said a communication error between its registrar MarkMonitor and GoDaddy Registry led the registry to shut off zoom.us; Zoom said it was not a hack or DDoS. A group called DarkStorm claimed it online without confirmation. Confirmed

NL: Zoom zei dat een communicatiefout tussen registrar MarkMonitor en GoDaddy Registry ertoe leidde dat het register zoom.us afsloot; Zoom zei dat het geen hack of DDoS was. Een groep DarkStorm eiste het online op zonder bevestiging.

Sources

  • GoDaddy Registry — zoom.us outage
  • TechRadar — Zoom outage April 2025
10 Mar 2025Xsocial network, website and appCyberattackClaimed

What happened

X went down repeatedly on 10 March 2025, with tens of thousands of outage reports in the US in the morning. X owner Elon Musk said the platform was hit by a 'massive cyberattack'. No cost figure was published.

NL: X lag op 10 maart 2025 meermaals plat, met tienduizenden storingsmeldingen in de VS in de ochtend. Eigenaar Elon Musk zei dat het platform getroffen werd door een 'massale cyberaanval'. Er werd geen kostenraming bekendgemaakt.

Company: X (formerly Twitter). Service: social network, website and app

Duration: several hours, intermittent. Where: Global

What caused it

Musk said it was a 'massive cyberattack' and suggested, without evidence, a link to Ukraine; a group calling itself Dark Storm Team claimed responsibility. Security Affairs noted the group had provided no evidence, and ZeroFox called a DDoS by the group plausible but unverified. X published no technical report. Claimed

NL: Musk sprak van een 'massale cyberaanval' en suggereerde zonder bewijs een link met Oekraïne; een groep die zich Dark Storm Team noemt, eiste de aanval op. Security Affairs merkte op dat de groep geen bewijs leverde, en ZeroFox noemde een DDoS door die groep aannemelijk maar niet bevestigd. X publiceerde geen technisch verslag.

Who is blamed

Dark Storm Team (described by Check Point Research as pro-Palestinian) claimed a DDoS attack on Telegram and offered no independent proof (Security Affairs, Daily Dot). Musk said the attack came from IP addresses in the 'Ukraine area' (his statement; no evidence published). Not confirmed by X or any authority. Claimed

1 Mar 2025MicrosoftOutlook and Microsoft 365 (Teams, Exchange Online)Technical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

Tens of thousands of users could not reach Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services; Downdetector logged more than 35,000 complaints.

NL: Tienduizenden gebruikers konden Outlook, Teams en andere Microsoft 365-diensten niet bereiken; Downdetector registreerde meer dan 35.000 klachten.

Duration: Several hours. Where: Global

What caused it

Microsoft said it reverted a suspected 'problematic code change'. It had not published a detailed report in the coverage found. Confirmed

NL: Microsoft zei een vermoedelijk 'problematische codewijziging' te hebben teruggedraaid. In de gevonden berichtgeving was geen gedetailleerd verslag gepubliceerd.

Sources

  • TechRepublic — Microsoft Outage: Tens of Thousands Unable to Access Outlook, Teams, Office 365 After 'Problematic Code Change'
26 Feb 2025SlackSlack messagingTechnical fault or changeReported

What happened

Slack users had trouble loading and using the workplace messaging service for most of a working day.

NL: Slack-gebruikers konden de berichtendienst het grootste deel van een werkdag moeilijk laden of gebruiken.

Company: Slack (Salesforce). Service: Slack messaging

Duration: About 9.5 hours (Events API effects lingered to next morning). Where: Global

What caused it

Reported: Pingdom and ThousandEyes say Slack attributed it to database maintenance combined with a latent defect in a caching system. Not seen in Slack's own post-mortem by this research. Reported

NL: Gemeld: Pingdom en ThousandEyes schrijven dat Slack het toeschreef aan onderhoud aan de databases in combinatie met een sluimerende fout in een cachingsysteem. Het eigen verslag van Slack werd niet geraadpleegd.

7–8 Feb 2025SonyPlayStation Network (sign-in, online play)Cause not publishedNot published

What happened

PlayStation Network went down worldwide; players could not sign in or play online. Push Square called it the biggest PSN outage since 2011.

NL: PlayStation Network lag wereldwijd plat; spelers konden niet inloggen of online spelen. Push Square noemde het de grootste PSN-storing sinds 2011.

Duration: About 20–24 hours (sources differ). Where: Global

What caused it

Sony only said there was an 'operational issue'. It has not published a cause. Speculation about an attack was not confirmed. Not published

NL: Sony sprak enkel van een 'operationeel probleem' en publiceerde geen oorzaak. Speculatie over een aanval werd niet bevestigd.

Background: 2024 outages people still refer to (5)
21 Nov 2024Blue Yondersupply-chain and workforce-scheduling softwareCyberattackReported

What happened

A ransomware attack on supply-chain software supplier Blue Yonder in November 2024 disrupted its customers. Starbucks said its scheduling and pay systems were hit (reports say staff pay had to be calculated manually); Morrisons reported problems with its warehouse management systems; Sainsbury's said it had contingencies in place and restored operations quickly (as reported by TechRepublic and others).

NL: Een ransomware-aanval op leverancier van supply-chainsoftware Blue Yonder in november 2024 verstoorde zijn klanten. Starbucks zei dat zijn rooster- en loonsystemen werden getroffen (volgens berichten moest het loon van het personeel handmatig worden berekend); Morrisons meldde problemen met zijn magazijnbeheersystemen; Sainsbury's zei dat het noodplannen had en de werking snel herstelde (zoals gemeld door TechRepublic en anderen).

Company: Blue Yonder (customers: Starbucks, Morrisons, Sainsbury's). Service: supply-chain and workforce-scheduling software

Duration: not verified; some customers reported problems for days. Where: US, UK

What caused it

Reported as a ransomware attack on Blue Yonder's managed-services hosted environment; its Azure public cloud was reportedly not affected. Blue Yonder said it worked with outside cybersecurity firms. Reported

NL: Gemeld als een ransomware-aanval op de gehoste beheerde-dienstenomgeving van Blue Yonder; de publieke Azure-cloud werd naar verluidt niet getroffen. Blue Yonder zei samen te werken met externe cyberbeveiligingsbedrijven.

Who is blamed

The Termite ransomware group claimed it on its leak site, saying it took 680 GB of data (claim). BleepingComputer said it could not independently confirm the link. Blue Yonder had not confirmed the claim. Claimed

Sources

  • CyberScoop — Termite ransomware, Blue Yonder disruption (Dec 2024)
  • BleepingComputer — Blue Yonder SaaS giant breached by Termite ransomware gang (Dec 2024)

19 Jul 2024CrowdStrike / Microsoft WindowsFalcon sensor on Windows PCs and servers (airlines, banks, hospitals)Technical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

A faulty content update for CrowdStrike's Falcon security software crashed Windows machines into boot loops worldwide. Reporting says more than 8 million Windows systems were affected, with disruption to airlines, banks and hospitals.

NL: Een foutieve inhoudsupdate van de beveiligingssoftware Falcon van CrowdStrike liet Windows-computers wereldwijd vastlopen in een herstartlus. Volgens de berichtgeving waren meer dan 8 miljoen Windows-systemen getroffen, met hinder voor luchtvaartmaatschappijen, banken en ziekenhuizen.

Duration: Hours to days (recovery needed manual fixes). Where: Global

What caused it

CrowdStrike's root cause analysis (6 Aug 2024) says a new template type defined 21 input fields while the code supplied only 20 values, causing an out-of-bounds memory read, and that a validator logic error let the file through. Not an attack. Confirmed

NL: In zijn oorzaakanalyse (6 augustus 2024) zegt CrowdStrike dat een nieuw sjabloontype 21 invoervelden definieerde terwijl de code er maar 20 doorgaf, wat een geheugenfout veroorzaakte, en dat een logische fout in de validatie het bestand doorliet. Geen aanval.

Sources

  • CrowdStrike — Channel File 291 Incident: Root Cause Analysis is Available (2024-08-06)
  • TechTarget — CrowdStrike details errors that led to mass IT outage
19 Jun 2024CDK Globaldealer management software used by about 15,000 car dealerships in…CyberattackReported

What happened

Two attacks on CDK Global in June 2024 took its dealer systems offline, so dealerships went back to pen and paper for sales, parts and financing; restoration came in stages around the start of July. Anderson Economic Group estimated losses to dealerships at roughly US$1 billion (an outside estimate, not a company figure).

NL: Twee aanvallen op CDK Global in juni 2024 legden de dealersystemen plat, waardoor autodealers terugvielen op pen en papier voor verkoop, onderdelen en financiering; het herstel verliep gefaseerd rond begin juli. Anderson Economic Group schatte de verliezen van de dealers op ongeveer 1 miljard dollar (een externe schatting, geen cijfer van het bedrijf).

Service: dealer management software used by about 15,000 car dealerships in North America

Duration: about two weeks, with restoration in stages from late June. Where: US, Canada

What caused it

CDK Global confirmed cyber incidents in June 2024 that took its dealer systems offline. Media reported (via sources) that ransomware was used; CDK's own wording in the sources seen was a 'cyber incident'. Reported

NL: CDK Global bevestigde cyberincidenten in juni 2024 die zijn dealersystemen platlegden. Media meldden op basis van bronnen dat ransomware werd gebruikt; CDK sprak zelf in de geraadpleegde bronnen van een 'cyberincident'.

Who is blamed

Media citing sources (Reuters, Bloomberg) and researchers named the BlackSuit group (not confirmed by CDK or an authority in the sources seen). Reports that CDK paid a ransom of about US$25 million were not confirmed by CDK. Reported

Sources

  • BleepingComputer — CDK Global cyberattack impacts thousands of US car dealerships (Jun 2024)
  • Fortune — CDK ransomware attack: car dealerships revert to paperwork (24 Jun 2024)
  • TechTarget — The CDK Global outage: explaining how it happened (2024)
22 Feb 2024AT&TNationwide wireless voice, 5G data, 911 accessTechnical fault or changeConfirmed

What happened

All voice and 5G data service on AT&T's wireless network went down across the US. The FCC said more than 125 million devices were affected, more than 92 million calls were blocked and more than 25,000 calls to 911 centres failed.

NL: Alle spraak- en 5G-datadiensten op het mobiele netwerk van AT&T vielen in de VS uit. Volgens de FCC waren meer dan 125 miljoen toestellen getroffen, werden meer dan 92 miljoen oproepen geblokkeerd en mislukten meer dan 25.000 oproepen naar noodcentrales.

Duration: About 12 hours to restore all commercial customers. Where: United States

What caused it

The FCC report said a network change with an equipment configuration error, not caught or peer-reviewed, put the network into 'protect mode'. Not an attack. Confirmed

NL: Volgens het FCC-rapport zette een netwerkwijziging met een configuratiefout, die niet was opgemerkt of door collega's nagekeken, het netwerk in 'beschermmodus'. Geen aanval.

Sources

  • Fierce Network — FCC says this is what caused AT&T's big outage in February
  • Broadband Breakfast — February AT&T Outage Blocked 92 Million Calls, FCC Says
21 Feb 2024Change HealthcareUS pharmacy claims, payments and healthcare billing networkCyberattackConfirmed

What happened

A ransomware attack on Change Healthcare from 21 February 2024 disrupted US claims processing. UnitedHealth estimated that 90% of the more than 70,000 US pharmacies using Change's platform had to modify their electronic claims processing (company estimate, as reported by Becker's). UnitedHealth's first-quarter 2024 results reported US$872 million of unfavourable cyberattack effects on earnings (company figure; media report it as US$593 million direct response costs and US$279 million business disruption).

NL: Een ransomware-aanval op Change Healthcare vanaf 21 februari 2024 verstoorde de verwerking van Amerikaanse betalingsaanvragen. UnitedHealth schatte dat 90 procent van de meer dan 70.000 Amerikaanse apotheken die het platform van Change gebruiken, hun elektronische verwerking moest aanpassen (schatting van het bedrijf, zoals gemeld door Becker's). In de resultaten voor het eerste kwartaal van 2024 meldde UnitedHealth 872 miljoen dollar aan ongunstige effecten van de cyberaanval op de winst (cijfer van het bedrijf; media splitsen dat op in 593 miljoen dollar directe herstelkosten en 279 miljoen dollar bedrijfsverstoring).

Company: Change Healthcare (UnitedHealth Group). Service: US pharmacy claims, payments and healthcare billing network

Duration: weeks to months. Where: US

What caused it

Change Healthcare confirmed a ransomware attack. UnitedHealth CEO Andrew Witty told a US Senate hearing that attackers got in through a server without multi-factor authentication. Confirmed

NL: Change Healthcare bevestigde een ransomware-aanval. UnitedHealth-ceo Andrew Witty zei op een hoorzitting in de Amerikaanse Senaat dat de aanvallers binnenraakten via een server zonder meerfactorauthenticatie.

Who is blamed

UnitedHealth/Change Healthcare attributed the attack to the ALPHV (BlackCat) group, and ALPHV also claimed it. Witty testified to the US Congress that UnitedHealth paid a US$22 million ransom in bitcoin (company CEO's own testimony). Confirmed

  • US SEC EDGAR (UnitedHealth) — UnitedHealth Group Q1 2024 results (Form 8-K exhibit) (Apr 2024)
  • CBS News — UnitedHealth CEO Senate hearing on Change Healthcare cyberattack (May 2024)
  • Axios — Ransomware attack wreaks havoc on prescription payments (1 Mar 2024)
  • Becker's Hospital Review — UnitedHealth says most pharmacies have 'effective workarounds' (Mar 2024)
  • MSSP Alert — UnitedHealth takes $872 million hit from BlackCat attack (Apr 2024)

What the pattern shows

  • Of the 32 platform and network outages (cloud, internet, telecom and online services), 22 were put down to a technical fault or change, 4 to a power or cooling failure and 6 have no published cause. None of them is blamed on a cyberattack in the sources seen. For 25 of the 32 the company or an authority confirmed the cause.
  • Fifteen of the 32 platform outages were at just three companies: Cloudflare (5); Google (5; counted together: Google and Google Cloud); Microsoft (5). Counted by company name only.
  • 4 outages were traced to physical problems in data centres (power or cooling), at Amazon, Google Cloud and Microsoft.
  • Of the 22 outages caused by cyberattacks, the company or an authority confirmed the attack itself in 20, but a culprit was formally named by an authority in only 1. In 11 the only name is a group's own claim, in 2 it is reported by media, and in 8 nobody is named (status in the sources seen).

A "Claimed" culprit is not a finding: this file records only that the claim was made. Counts are made from the cards above, not from outside statistics.
