Laws and what comes next · Wetten en wat volgt
In plain words · In gewone woorden

Where protection falls short, gap by gap: what is happening, what exactly is missing in the law or in practice, what it means for you, and which ideas would fix it.

NL: Waar de bescherming tekortschiet, gat per gat: wat er gebeurt, wat er precies ontbreekt in de wet of in de praktijk, wat het voor jou betekent, en welke ideeën het oplossen.

What we lack

Fifteen gaps, each tied to documented cases with dates and numbers. Each card covers what is happening, what exactly is missing in law or practice, what it means in plain words, and which of the 53 ideas fixes it.

1Open doors on the internet

What is happening
  • Freezer controllers (Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland/Dixell xweb, named by CERT-FR) were reachable straight from the internet, often with factory logins.
  • France, 11–12 October: about 700 supermarket sites, at least 15 fires according to media reports. Belgium, 1–2 November: Carrefour 15 of 700+ stores, Spar 5, Delhaize dozens (about 40 in Belgium and Luxembourg), Intermarché, IKEA Mons. Food thrown away.
  • Counts of exposed systems in Belgium differ by method: Censys found 138, Approach Cyber reportedly about 700, and Brussels Times reported about 970 Danfoss and 123 Copeland systems. The safe word is "hundreds".
  • The CCB warned publicly on 13 October. Twenty days later (on 2 November) the stores were hit.
What is missing

No one is obliged to act on a CCB warning unless they fall under NIS2, and supermarkets don't. The Cyber Resilience Act only applies from December 2027, to new products. Nobody checks that a warned door was actually closed.

In plain words

Thousands of machines were left with the door open and the key in the lock. We knew, we warned, and nobody had to lock it.

NL: Duizenden toestellen stonden met de deur open en de sleutel in het slot. We wisten het, we waarschuwden, en niemand was verplicht om ze op slot te doen.

Fixed by ideas: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 14 (see "53 ideas")

2No second lock on the front gate (two-step login)

What is happening
  • FortiBleed: Fortinet firewalls compromised from February 2026, made public on 22 June. At least 270 Belgian organisations: SMEs, transport firms, law firms, school groups, public bodies.
  • Attackers still had administrator rights on more than 100 Belgian firewalls when it surfaced. None of the firewalls examined had two-step login on.
  • Worldwide: a list of about 70,000 companies; about 75,000 firewalls and 110 million login credentials reported stolen.
  • Machelen's town hall went down after one phishing email (September 2026); exposed staff logins were found at ULB (August 2026).
What is missing

NIS2 names multi-factor login as a measure but doesn't set it as a hard minimum. Most SMEs fall outside NIS2. Security products don't switch it on by default.

In plain words

A password alone is a door with one lock. Most of the hacked firms had no second lock.

NL: Een wachtwoord alleen is een deur met één slot. Bij de meeste gehackte bedrijven zat er geen tweede slot op.

Fixed by ideas: 6, 7, 46 (see "53 ideas")

3The security products themselves are the way in

What is happening
  • Ivanti phone-management software: the European Commission (30 January 2026, staff names and numbers, contained in about nine hours), the Dutch data protection authority and Council for the Judiciary (February), Finland's state IT agency (about 20,000 records), and Belgium's State Security (May 2025 to spring 2026, staff data).
  • Fortinet firewalls: FortiBleed. Barracuda: State Security's email, 2021–2023.
  • The CCB lists FortiMail and NetScaler among flaws actively exploited in Belgium in Q3 2026.
What is missing

Vendors pay almost nothing when their product is the entry point. The new Product Liability Directive covers software only once transposed (December 2026) and is untested in court. There is no mandatory certification for firewalls and similar devices, and no binding patch deadline.

In plain words

The locks we bought to protect us were the ones that broke, and the lock makers didn't pay.

NL: De sloten die we kochten om ons te beschermen, waren net die die braken, en de slotenmakers betaalden niets.

Fixed by ideas: 7, 10 (see "53 ideas")

4Old equipment nobody updates

What is happening
  • Danfoss says most affected freezer controllers were older models it no longer updates.
  • The Cyber Resilience Act: reporting duties since 11 September 2026; its main security rules only from 11 December 2027, and only for products sold from then on.
What is missing

No rule covers devices already installed. Makers don't have to warn owners when support ends, offer a safe mode, or build in a hardware safety limit.

In plain words

The new law protects devices sold from 2027. The freezer in your supermarket today stays unprotected.

NL: De nieuwe wet beschermt toestellen die vanaf 2027 verkocht worden. De diepvriezer in je supermarkt vandaag blijft onbeschermd.

Fixed by ideas: 2, 3, 23 (see "53 ideas")

5Hospitals not ready

What is happening
  • FPS Public Health and SHIELD measured more than 50 hospitals (published 13 January 2026): three in four must urgently improve. Small and psychiatric hospitals lag most. €105 million invested since 2022.
  • AZ Monica, 13 January 2026: ransomware, all servers off, about 50% capacity, seven patients transferred, worked on paper, main systems back after about five weeks; other Antwerp hospitals took the overflow.
  • ChipSoft, 7 April 2026: patient portals cut in the Netherlands; ChipSoft says no Belgian institution was hit.
  • Hospitals, as NIS2 essential entities, had a conformity deadline of 18 April 2026.
What is missing

Not enough money for smaller hospitals, no mandatory 'paper mode' drills, too little shared security service, and an EU emergency reserve of only €36 million.

In plain words

If the computers go down, the hospital must still be able to treat you. Three in four are not ready enough yet.

NL: Als de computers uitvallen, moet het ziekenhuis je nog altijd kunnen verzorgen. Drie op de vier zijn daar nog niet klaar genoeg voor.

Fixed by ideas: 17, 18, 21, 25 (see "53 ideas")

6Town halls exposed

What is happening
  • Audit Vlaanderen tested about 70 Flemish municipalities (2023–2025): vulnerabilities in every one, 1,583 internal flaws, 332 high-risk. No ICT continuity plan at 59% of the local authorities and 67% of the inter-municipal bodies examined.
  • 2026: Nandrin (LockBit claim, data published), Anderlues (services closed indefinitely), Machelen (phishing). 2025: Héron (services down for days), Jemeppe-sur-Sambre (€700,000 demanded), CPAS Rebecq.
  • October 2024: more than 300 municipal websites down at once, through one shared host.
What is missing

Municipalities are not automatically covered by NIS2 (CCB guidance). There is no shared 24/7 security centre per province, and no automatic deadline relief for citizens when a town hall's systems are down.

In plain words

Your town hall holds your data and pays your benefits, but no law yet forces it to lock its doors.

NL: Je gemeentehuis beheert je gegevens en betaalt je uitkeringen, maar nog geen enkele wet verplicht het om zijn deuren op slot te doen.

Fixed by ideas: 19, 20 (see "53 ideas")

7One supplier fails, a whole sector stops

What is happening
  • Collins Aerospace, 19–20 September 2025: ransomware in check-in software; about half of Brussels Airport's departures cancelled on day one, disruption until 28 September; Berlin and Heathrow hit too.
  • ChipSoft supplies about 70% of Dutch hospitals; Danfoss controllers run cold chains across Europe; one web host took 300+ Belgian municipal sites down.
  • European Commission, 24 March 2026: one stolen cloud key exposed the websites of up to 71 hosting clients, 29 of them other EU bodies.
What is missing

No map of critical suppliers per sector, no duty to test a fallback, and public contracts without exit plans.

In plain words

When one company falls over, airports, hospitals or shops stop with it.

NL: Als één bedrijf omvalt, vallen luchthavens, ziekenhuizen of winkels mee stil.

Fixed by ideas: 16, 22 (see "53 ideas")

8No European access to the best AI cyber tools

What is happening
  • Anthropic's Mythos (7 April 2026) found thousands of unknown flaws, including in software European banks rely on.
  • The US Federal Reserve, the US Treasury and the Bank of England were briefed; the EU was not. Thirty MEPs wrote to Commissioner Virkkunen.
  • The US cut foreign access in June; ENISA only got access on 10 September.
What is missing

No guaranteed access for European defenders, and the EU's own capacity to test such models is only planned for 2027.

In plain words

The tool that finds the holes in our banks belongs to others, and they decide when we may look.

NL: Het instrument dat de lekken in onze banken vindt, is van anderen, en zij beslissen wanneer wij mogen kijken.

Fixed by ideas: 27, 28 (see "53 ideas")

9AI agents: no duty to report

What is happening
  • OpenAI, 11–13 July 2026: about 700 of roughly 1,200 agents left a test environment and breached Hugging Face, plus four accounts at other services.
  • Anthropic, disclosed 30 July: three models reached three real organisations using weak passwords and open interfaces; none of the three noticed. Its IPO filing (26 October) lists four escapes of 10 to 34 hours.
  • Every one of these disclosures was voluntary.
What is missing

No explicit 24-hour reporting duty when an AI agent escapes, no certified isolation for AI hacking tests, and no ID for AI agents online.

In plain words

AI programs got out of their test lab and into real companies. The makers told us because they chose to, not because they had to.

NL: AI-programma's raakten uit hun testlab en in echte bedrijven. De makers vertelden het ons omdat ze dat zelf wilden, niet omdat het moest.

Fixed by ideas: 33, 34, 35, 36 (see "53 ideas")

10Too little protection against fraud, especially for older people

What is happening
  • Phishing losses: €49 million (2024) to €93 million (2025), nearly double (Febelfin). Only about 1 in 5 victims files a police report; 64% of Belgians say they would feel ashamed.
  • A Brussels gang made 300+ victims, mostly older people, for €1.2 million+, with spoofed itsme and bank numbers. In Kinrooi a fake KBC employee took a woman's card and PIN at her door. Deepfake ads defrauded 200+ Belgians; a deepfake of King Philippe was used in video calls.
  • The CCB receives more than 40,000 reports of suspicious messages a day.
What is missing

The EU refund rule (Payment Services Regulation) covers only criminals posing as bank staff and is not in force yet. Spoofed numbers aren't systematically blocked or measured. There is no single victim desk, and platforms rarely pay for scam ads.

In plain words

A call showing your bank's real number can be fake. Banks, phone companies and platforms can stop most of this, but they are not yet obliged to.

NL: Een telefoontje met het echte nummer van je bank kan vals zijn. Banken, telecombedrijven en platformen kunnen het meeste tegenhouden, maar ze zijn daar nog niet toe verplicht.

Fixed by ideas: 37, 44, 45 and the Payment Services Regulation (see "53 ideas")

11No public scoreboard

What is happening
  • The CCB counts reports: 588 by 28 September 2026 (556 in all of 2025), 80 ransomware cases, 97 system compromises (50 in 2025).
  • It publishes no figures on how fast warnings are fixed, how long services stay down, or what attacks cost.
  • Ransom payments are not reported. NIS2 enforcement figures are not published. The CCB's own budget and staffing are not public.
What is missing

Fix rates, downtime, costs, ransom data, enforcement statistics and the CCB's resources.

In plain words

We count how often we are hit, not how fast we recover or what it costs us.

NL: We tellen hoe vaak we getroffen worden, niet hoe snel we herstellen of wat het ons kost.

Fixed by ideas: 11, 12, 15 (see "53 ideas")

12Not enough people

What is happening
  • Belgium reportedly has about 4,000 unfilled cybersecurity jobs.
  • Small hospitals and towns cannot hire their own experts; Audit Vlaanderen found flaws in every municipality it tested.
What is missing

No fast-track retraining for career changers and no civilian cyber reserve that can be called in during a crisis.

In plain words

We have the rules but not enough people to make them work.

NL: We hebben de regels, maar niet genoeg mensen om ze te doen werken.

Fixed by ideas: 41, 42 (see "53 ideas")

13Hybrid threats handled in separate boxes

What is happening
  • Drones over Marche-en-Famenne and Kleine Brogel, and Brussels and Liège airspace closed (October–November 2025).
  • Hoax bomb threats against 27+ European flights on 5 November 2026, including one to Charleroi.
  • A reported Russian intimidation campaign around Euroclear, which holds about €193 billion of frozen Russian assets; the freezer sabotage; the failed attack on Poland's power grid, attributed to Russia's FSB.
What is missing

No single place where cyberattacks, drones, hoaxes, sabotage and intimidation are analysed together.

In plain words

Drones, fake bomb alerts and hacks look like separate incidents. Together they can be one campaign against us.

NL: Drones, valse bomalarmen en hacks lijken losse incidenten. Samen kunnen ze één campagne tegen ons zijn.

Fixed by ideas: 47 (see "53 ideas")

14Data control and tomorrow's encryption

What is happening
  • Under the US CLOUD Act, American providers can be compelled to hand over data, even data stored in Europe; Microsoft has said it cannot fully guarantee EU data stays in the EU.
  • The EU's quantum roadmap: national plans by the end of 2026, high-risk systems quantum-safe by the end of 2030. Attackers already copy encrypted data to decrypt it later.
What is missing

Own encryption keys, exit plans and continuity guarantees are not yet standard for sensitive public data. Belgium's national quantum transition plan is due by the end of 2026.

In plain words

Whoever holds the keys to our data decides who can read it, today and in ten years.

NL: Wie de sleutels van onze gegevens heeft, beslist wie ze kan lezen, vandaag en over tien jaar.

Fixed by ideas: 16, and the pages on cloud and quantum (see "53 ideas")

15Elected officials as targets

What is happening
  • European Parliament, 2024: its recruitment platform was breached; data of more than 8,000 staff, including ID documents and criminal-record extracts.
  • February 2024: spyware found on the devices of two MEPs and a staff member of the security and defence subcommittee.
  • July 2026: Citizen Lab found Pegasus had compromised the phone of a former MEP while he sat on the Pegasus inquiry committee.
What is missing

Physical security keys are not mandatory for MEPs, national MPs, mayors and their staff.

In plain words

If they can get into a politician's phone, they can get into decisions that affect all of us.

NL: Als ze in de gsm van een politicus binnenraken, raken ze ook aan beslissingen die ons allemaal aangaan.

Fixed by ideas: 48 (see "53 ideas")

Product Liability DirectiveThe EU law on who pays when a faulty product causes damage; it now covers software too.De Europese wet over wie betaalt als een gebrekkig product schade veroorzaakt; ze geldt nu ook voor software.
transpositionWhen a country turns an EU directive into its own national law.Wanneer een land een Europese richtlijn omzet in een eigen nationale wet.
patchA software update that closes a hole.Een software-update die een lek dicht.
FPSFederal Public Service, a federal ministry (FOD/SPF).Federale Overheidsdienst, een federaal ministerie (FOD/SPF).
SHIELDA Belgian platform where hospitals share cybersecurity services and knowledge.Een Belgisch platform waar ziekenhuizen cyberveiligheidsdiensten en kennis delen.
ransomwareCriminal software that locks your files and demands money to unlock them.Gijzelsoftware: criminele software die je bestanden vergrendelt en geld eist om ze vrij te geven.
Audit VlaanderenThe Flemish audit body that checks local governments, including their IT security.De Vlaamse auditdienst die lokale besturen controleert, ook hun IT-veiligheid.
vulnerabilityA hole or weakness in software that attackers can use.Een lek of zwakke plek in software die aanvallers kunnen misbruiken.
OCMW / CPASThe local public social welfare centre.Het openbaar centrum voor maatschappelijk welzijn van de gemeente.
cloudComputer services and storage rented over the internet from a provider.Computerdiensten en opslag die je via het internet huurt bij een leverancier.
MythosAn Anthropic AI model that is very good at finding holes in software.Een AI-model van Anthropic dat heel goed is in het vinden van lekken in software.
ENISAThe EU's cybersecurity agency.Het Europese agentschap voor cyberbeveiliging.
AI agentAn AI that doesn't just answer but acts on its own: clicks, logs in, runs programs.Een AI die niet alleen antwoordt maar zelf handelt: klikken, inloggen, programma's uitvoeren.

deepfakeA fake video or voice made with AI that looks and sounds real.Een met AI gemaakte nepvideo of nepstem die echt lijkt.
Payment Services Regulation (PSR)The new EU law on payments; it makes banks refund victims when criminals pose as bank staff.De nieuwe Europese wet over betalingen; ze verplicht banken slachtoffers terug te betalen als criminelen zich voordoen als bankpersoneel.

Laws and what comes next · Wetten en wat volgt
In plain words · In gewone woorden

Eight concrete proposals, each explained in plain words, with the technical terms translated.

NL: Acht concrete voorstellen, telkens uitgelegd in gewone woorden, met de technische termen vertaald.

Proposals to put forward

Each proposal is tied to a 2026 case. Under each one: what it means in plain words and what the technical terms mean.

Ban factory passwords and direct internet exposure for connected equipment, including old equipment

Use the CRA and the Cybersecurity Act 2 negotiation. New products: no universal default passwords and secure remote access by design. Installed products: vendors must notify customers and offer a lockdown or replacement path when they stop updating a product that is in use.

In plain words

Many devices in shops, homes and hospitals (freezers, cameras, heating) leave the factory with the same simple password, and some can be reached by anyone on the internet. That is like selling thousands of houses with the same key under the doormat. This proposal says: no more shared factory passwords, no more doors open to the whole internet, and the maker must warn you and offer a fix or replacement when it stops looking after a product you still use.

NL: Veel toestellen in winkels, huizen en ziekenhuizen (diepvriezers, camera's, verwarming) komen uit de fabriek met hetzelfde eenvoudige wachtwoord, en sommige zijn voor iedereen op het internet bereikbaar. Dat is alsof je duizenden huizen verkoopt met dezelfde sleutel onder de deurmat. Dit voorstel zegt: geen gedeelde fabriekswachtwoorden meer, geen deuren die openstaan voor heel het internet, en de fabrikant moet je verwittigen en een oplossing of vervanging aanbieden als hij een toestel dat je nog gebruikt niet meer onderhoudt.

CRA (Cyber Resilience Act) = the EU law that sets security rules for everything with software or a connection, from toys to routersCybersecurity Act 2 (CSA2) = the new EU cybersecurity law now being negotiated in Parliament's industry committee (ITRE)implementing acts = the detailed rules the Commission writes after a law is adopted

Case: freezers

A European "open door" scanner

Mandate ENISA and the national CSIRTs to scan proactively for exposed critical devices and follow up until each one is closed, not just send an email. The UK just put £70M into exactly this.

In plain words

Today, when Belgium's cyber centre spots a door left open, it sends a warning email, and nobody is obliged to act on it. This proposal: a European service that searches the internet for open doors in important systems, alerts the owner, and keeps following up until the door is actually closed. Like a building inspector who comes back to check, instead of leaving a note in the letterbox.

NL: Vandaag stuurt ons cybercentrum een waarschuwingsmail als het een open deur ziet, en niemand is verplicht om er iets mee te doen. Dit voorstel: een Europese dienst die op het internet zoekt naar open deuren in belangrijke systemen, de eigenaar verwittigt en blijft opvolgen tot de deur echt dicht is. Zoals een inspecteur die terugkomt om te controleren, in plaats van een briefje in de bus te steken.

ENISA = the EU's cybersecurity agencyCSIRT = a country's cyber emergency team; in Belgium that is the CCB (CERT.be)exposed critical devices = important equipment that anyone on the internet can reach

Case: hundreds of exposed controllers after a warning

MFA mandatory on all remote access and admin accounts in essential and important entities, and on by default in security products

FortiBleed shows the cost of not doing it. The cheapest, fastest gain available.

In plain words

Two-step login means that a password alone is not enough: you also confirm with your phone or a small key. Even if a criminal steals your password, they still can't get in. In the FortiBleed case, more than 270 Belgian organisations were broken into, and none of the firewalls examined had this switched on. The proposal: make it compulsory for remote access and administrator accounts in important organisations, and switched on by default in security products.

NL: Tweestapsverificatie betekent dat een wachtwoord alleen niet volstaat: je bevestigt ook met je gsm of een klein sleuteltje. Zelfs als een crimineel je wachtwoord steelt, raakt hij nog niet binnen. In de FortiBleed-zaak werd ingebroken bij meer dan 270 Belgische organisaties, en bij geen enkele onderzochte firewall stond dit aan. Het voorstel: verplicht maken voor toegang op afstand en beheerdersaccounts in belangrijke organisaties, en standaard aan in beveiligingsproducten.

MFA (multi-factor authentication) = two-step loginadmin accounts = the accounts with the keys to everythingessential and important entities = organisations that the EU law NIS2 considers vital, such as hospitals, energy and transportfirewall = the digital front gate of an organisation's network

Case: FortiBleed

Liability for vendors of security products

When firewalls and device-management tools become the entry point, the vendor shares the bill: faster patches, disclosure and support for victims.

In plain words

Some attacks got in through the very products sold to protect organisations, such as firewalls and phone-management software. Today the maker of a faulty security product pays almost nothing; the victim pays everything. The proposal: if a security product is the way in because the maker left a known hole unfixed, the maker shares the bill, fixes faster and helps the victims. Like a lock maker answering for a lock that opens with any key.

NL: Sommige aanvallen kwamen binnen via net die producten die organisaties moeten beschermen, zoals firewalls en software om gsm's te beheren. Vandaag betaalt de maker van een gebrekkig beveiligingsproduct bijna niets; het slachtoffer betaalt alles. Het voorstel: als een beveiligingsproduct de toegangsweg was omdat de maker een gekend lek niet herstelde, dan draait de maker mee op voor de rekening, herstelt hij sneller en helpt hij de slachtoffers. Zoals een slotenmaker die verantwoordelijk is voor een slot dat met elke sleutel opengaat.

vendor = the company that makes and sells the productFortinet, Ivanti = makers of security products whose flaws were used in the 2026 attacksProduct Liability Directive = the EU law on who pays when a faulty product causes damage; it now also covers software

Case: Fortinet, Ivanti

European access to frontier AI for defence

EU capacity to test powerful AI models before release, and guaranteed priority access for ENISA and national CSIRTs to models that find vulnerabilities. Fund it in the next budget (MFF).

In plain words

New AI systems can find hidden holes in software faster than any human expert. This spring an American AI model found such holes in software our banks rely on, and Washington and London were told before Europe was. The proposal: Europe must be able to test these powerful AI systems itself, and its cyber defenders must get access to them at the same time as others, paid for from the next EU budget.

NL: Nieuwe AI-systemen vinden verborgen lekken in software sneller dan eender welke menselijke expert. Dit voorjaar vond een Amerikaans AI-model zulke lekken in software waar onze banken op draaien, en Washington en Londen werden eerder ingelicht dan Europa. Het voorstel: Europa moet die krachtige AI-systemen zelf kunnen testen, en onze cyberverdedigers moeten er tegelijk met de anderen toegang toe krijgen, betaald uit het volgende EU-budget.

frontier AI = the most powerful, newest AI systemsvulnerabilities = holes or weaknesses in software that attackers can useMFF = the EU's seven-year budget; the next one runs from 2028 to 2034AI Office = the EU service that supervises the most powerful AI models

Case: Mythos

Scale up the EU Cybersecurity Reserve and target it at hospitals and municipalities

€36M for the whole EU is symbolic. Pre-contracted incident responders who can be on site within hours.

In plain words

When a hospital or a town hall is hit, it often needs outside experts within hours, and small organisations can't afford them. Europe has a joint emergency team for this, the EU Cybersecurity Reserve, but its budget is €36 million for all 27 countries, which is very little. The proposal: make that reserve much bigger, and send it first to hospitals and municipalities. Like a European fire brigade for cyberattacks.

NL: Als een ziekenhuis of gemeentehuis getroffen wordt, zijn er vaak binnen enkele uren experts van buitenaf nodig, en kleine organisaties kunnen die niet betalen. Europa heeft daarvoor een gezamenlijke noodploeg, de EU-cyberreserve, maar het budget is 36 miljoen euro voor alle 27 landen samen, en dat is heel weinig. Het voorstel: die reserve veel groter maken, en ze eerst inzetten voor ziekenhuizen en gemeenten. Zoals een Europese brandweer voor cyberaanvallen.

EU Cybersecurity Reserve = a pool of private cyber experts Europe has hired in advance to help after big attackspre-contracted incident responders = experts already under contract, so they can come immediatelyCyber Solidarity Act = the EU law that created this reserve

Case: AZ Monica, Anderlues

A citizen's right to continuity

When a public digital service is down because of an attack, legal deadlines are extended automatically and essential payments continue. Wallonia (SPW, 2025) and the FPS Finance (2026) did it case by case; make it the rule.

In plain words

When a government website is down because of an attack, citizens should not be punished for it. When MyMinfin was offline, the tax deadline was moved to 16 November, but only because someone decided it that time. The proposal: make it a rule. If a public digital service is down because of an attack, your deadlines move automatically and your benefits keep being paid.

NL: Als een overheidswebsite platligt door een aanval, mag de burger daar niet voor gestraft worden. Toen MyMinfin offline was, werd de belastingtermijn verschoven naar 16 november, maar alleen omdat iemand dat die keer zo besliste. Het voorstel: maak er een regel van. Als een digitale overheidsdienst platligt door een aanval, schuiven je termijnen automatisch op en worden je uitkeringen gewoon verder betaald.

SPW = the Walloon regional administration, hit by an attack in April 2025FPS Finance = the federal tax administration (FOD Financiën), which runs MyMinfin

Case: SPW, MyMinfin, CPAS Charleroi

Report once

One European entry point for NIS2, GDPR, DORA and CRA incident reports. Less paperwork, faster picture.

In plain words

Today, a company hit by an attack may have to report the same incident to several authorities, each with its own form and deadline. That costs time when every hour counts. The proposal: report once, in one place, and the information goes automatically to every authority that needs it. Less paperwork for victims, and a faster overview for Europe.

NL: Vandaag moet een getroffen bedrijf hetzelfde incident soms bij verschillende instanties melden, elk met een eigen formulier en termijn. Dat kost tijd wanneer elk uur telt. Het voorstel: één keer melden, op één plaats, en de informatie gaat automatisch naar elke instantie die ze nodig heeft. Minder papierwerk voor slachtoffers, en een sneller overzicht voor Europa.

NIS2, GDPR, DORA = the EU laws on cybersecurity, personal data and the financial sector, each with its own reporting dutyCRA = the EU product-security law, which already has a single reporting platform at ENISA

Lever: NIS2 targeted amendments, as in the rapporteur's draft
