Laws and what comes next · Wetten en wat volgt
In plain words · In gewone woorden

Fifty concrete ideas. For each: what exactly changes, the 2026 case that proves it is needed, the law it would go through, who must act, and how we will know it worked.

NL: Vijftig concrete ideeën. Telkens: wat er precies verandert, het geval uit 2026 dat bewijst dat het nodig is, via welke wet het kan, wie moet handelen, en hoe we weten dat het gewerkt heeft.

5 · Fifty-three ideas to make Europe and Belgium safer

Grouped by theme. They go further than the Commission's current proposals, because the 2026 incidents showed where the rules fall short.

The top five, plus one for older people. If only a few can be named: 1 (no factory passwords or open interfaces, including installed devices), 5 (a European scanner that gets open doors closed), 6 (two-step login mandatory on all remote access), 27 (European access to frontier AI for defence), 33 (AI labs report agent escapes within 24 hours). For older people: refund victims when the system was faked (spoofed bank numbers, cloned bank sites, SIM swaps), and make banks call back before out-of-character transfers or share the loss. Platforms pay for scam ads they kept running after a report.

A · Close the open doors

Freezers, firewalls, AI agents: the same weak entry points.
  1. 1Ban internet-facing management interfaces without authenticated, encrypted access
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Many machines in shops and buildings, like freezers, heating and cameras, can be controlled over the internet. Today some of them can be reached by anyone in the world, like a front door left wide open on a busy street. This idea says: only the right people, with a proper key, may get in from outside. Everyone else stays out.

    NL: Veel toestellen in winkels en gebouwen, zoals diepvriezers, verwarming en camera's, kun je via het internet bedienen. Vandaag kan iedereen ter wereld bij sommige ervan, zoals een voordeur die wagenwijd openstaat in een drukke straat. Dit idee zegt: alleen de juiste mensen, met een echte sleutel, mogen van buitenaf binnen. Alle anderen blijven buiten.

    What exactly
    Remote management of OT, building, cold-chain and energy controllers only through authenticated, encrypted channels (VPN or equivalent). No admin page reachable from the open internet by default.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The freezer controllers hit in France (about 700 sites, 11–12 Oct) and Belgium (2 Nov) were reachable straight from the internet; counts of exposed systems in Belgium alone range from 138 to about 1,100, depending on the method.
    Legal route
    Cyber Resilience Act harmonised standards (Annex I already demands secure-by-default and protection against unauthorised access); NIS2 Art. 21 risk measures for covered operators.
    Who acts
    Commission and European standardisation bodies; manufacturers; ITRE in the Cybersecurity Act 2 and NIS2 amendments.
    Success looks like
    A scan of Belgian address space finds close to zero exposed controllers within 12 months.
    EU · CRA
  2. 2Make "default password" a legal defect, including for products already sold
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Many devices leave the factory with the same simple password, like 'admin', and the same one is on thousands of devices. That's like a building where every apartment opens with the same key. This idea bans that, and forces makers to make you choose your own password, even on devices you already own.

    NL: Veel toestellen komen uit de fabriek met hetzelfde eenvoudige wachtwoord, zoals 'admin', en datzelfde wachtwoord staat op duizenden toestellen. Dat is als een gebouw waar elk appartement met dezelfde sleutel opengaat. Dit idee verbiedt dat, en verplicht fabrikanten om je een eigen wachtwoord te laten kiezen, ook op toestellen die je al hebt.

    What exactly
    Universal default passwords banned outright. For devices already installed, the manufacturer must ship an update that forces a unique password at the next login, within six months of a known attack campaign.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Attackers tried default admin credentials on internet-facing Danfoss controllers.
    Legal route
    CRA Annex I (secure default configuration, applies to new products from 11 Dec 2027); the new Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853, which treats software and missing security updates as possible defects, transposed by December 2026.
    Who acts
    Manufacturers; national market surveillance authorities; Belgian transposition of the Product Liability Directive.
    Success looks like
    Every affected model has a forced-password-change update available, and its uptake is reported.
    EU · CRA / Product Liability
  3. 3End-of-support duty
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    When you buy a smart device, you should know how long the maker will keep fixing its security, like a guarantee on a car. And when that ends, the maker must warn you a year in advance and either lock the device safely or offer you a replacement. No more devices quietly left unprotected.

    NL: Als je een slim toestel koopt, moet je weten hoe lang de fabrikant de beveiliging blijft herstellen, zoals de garantie op een auto. En als dat stopt, moet de fabrikant je een jaar vooraf verwittigen en het toestel ofwel veilig afsluiten, ofwel een vervanging aanbieden. Geen toestellen meer die stilletjes onbeschermd achterblijven.

    What exactly
    The support period printed at the point of sale, a 12-month warning to owners before updates stop, and at the end either a final update that shuts remote access or a trade-in offer.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Danfoss says most affected freezer controllers were older models it no longer updates.
    Legal route
    CRA support-period rules (generally at least five years), extended by amendment or delegated act with a notification and safe-mode duty.
    Who acts
    Commission, manufacturers.
    Success looks like
    No unsupported device in shops or hospitals still has open remote access.
    EU · CRA amendment
  4. 4"Open door orders"
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Today, when the national cyber centre sees a dangerous open door, it can only send a warning, and nobody has to listen. This idea gives it the power to say: close this within 72 hours, or pay a fine. Like a fire inspector who can close a building that has no emergency exit.

    NL: Vandaag kan het nationale cybercentrum alleen een waarschuwing sturen als het een gevaarlijke open deur ziet, en niemand moet luisteren. Dit idee geeft het de macht om te zeggen: doe dit binnen 72 uur dicht, of betaal een boete. Zoals een brandweerinspecteur die een gebouw zonder nooduitgang kan laten sluiten.

    What exactly
    A legal power for the CCB to order a critical internet exposure closed within 72 hours, with escalating fines. For public bodies, binding instructions, published in anonymised form.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The CCB warned publicly on 13 October; Belgian stores were hit on 2 November. Twenty days, and nobody was obliged to act.
    Legal route
    NIS2 supervisory powers (binding instructions) extended to owners of critical devices outside NIS2, through the targeted NIS2 amendments; the Belgian NIS2 law.
    Who acts
    CCB; federal Parliament for the Belgian law; ITRE for the EU text.
    Success looks like
    The median time from CCB warning to closure is published and falls below one week.
    EU · NIS2 targeted amendments
  5. 5A European exposure scanner
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    A European service that searches the internet, day and night, for important machines left open to attack, and keeps chasing the owner until the door is closed. Like a neighbourhood patrol that doesn't just spot an open window but comes back to check it's shut.

    NL: Een Europese dienst die dag en nacht op het internet zoekt naar belangrijke toestellen die openstaan voor aanvallen, en de eigenaar blijft opvolgen tot de deur dicht is. Zoals een buurtpatrouille die niet alleen een open raam opmerkt, maar terugkomt om te kijken of het dicht is.

    What exactly
    ENISA and the national CSIRTs continuously scan the EU's internet space for exposed critical devices and known-exploited flaws. Each finding goes to the national CSIRT, which tracks it until it is closed.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    One security firm counted about 700 exposed Belgian controllers in days. The UK just put £70 million into a National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Centre.
    Legal route
    Cybersecurity Act 2 (new ENISA tasks) and the Cyber Solidarity Act's European Cybersecurity Alert System; funding from Digital Europe and the next EU budget.
    Who acts
    ENISA, CCB, ITRE.
    Success looks like
    A monthly public count of exposures found and closed, per country.
    EU · CSA2 ENISA mandate
  6. 6MFA mandatory on all remote and admin access
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Two-step login means a password alone is not enough: you also confirm with your phone or a small key, like the code your bank sends you. Even if a criminal steals your password, they can't get in. This idea makes it compulsory for anyone who logs in from outside to important systems.

    NL: Tweestapsverificatie betekent dat een wachtwoord alleen niet volstaat: je bevestigt ook met je gsm of een klein sleuteltje, zoals de code die je bank je stuurt. Zelfs als een crimineel je wachtwoord steelt, raakt hij niet binnen. Dit idee maakt dat verplicht voor iedereen die van buitenaf inlogt op belangrijke systemen.

    What exactly
    Two-step login on all remote access, VPN, firewall and administrator accounts. Phishing-resistant keys or passkeys for administrators and public officials.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    FortiBleed: 270+ Belgian organisations hacked, and none of the firewalls examined had two-step login. Machelen went down after one phishing email.
    Legal route
    NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j) already names multi-factor authentication as a measure: make it an explicit minimum in the targeted amendments or an implementing act; CyFun Basic for others.
    Who acts
    All NIS2 entities and public bodies; CCB as supervisor.
    Success looks like
    Coverage of two-step login reported in every NIS2 inspection; 100% for remote and admin access.
    EU / BE
  7. 7Mandatory certification for edge devices
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    The digital 'front gates' of hospitals, town halls and companies, called firewalls, must carry a European safety label before the government buys them, like the CE mark on a toy or a car's safety test. And they must come with the second lock switched on from day one.

    NL: De digitale 'voordeuren' van ziekenhuizen, gemeentehuizen en bedrijven, firewalls genoemd, moeten een Europees veiligheidslabel hebben voor de overheid ze koopt, zoals de CE-markering op speelgoed of de keuring van een auto. En ze moeten vanaf dag één met het tweede slot aan geleverd worden.

    What exactly
    Firewalls, VPN gateways and device-management tools sold to public bodies and essential entities must hold an EU cybersecurity certificate, ship with two-step login on, and meet fixed patch deadlines for actively exploited flaws.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Fortinet (FortiBleed), Ivanti (the Commission, State Security, the Dutch data watchdog) and Barracuda (State Security, earlier) were all the way in.
    Legal route
    Cybersecurity Act 2 certification (the ITRE rapporteur proposes certification mandatory by default); the CRA already puts firewalls among the 'important products' that need stricter conformity assessment.
    Who acts
    ITRE, Commission, ENISA.
    Success looks like
    Certified products are required in public tenders for these categories.
    EU · CSA2 (rapporteur's "mandatory by default")
  8. 8Bring large food retail into NIS2
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Big supermarket chains feed millions of people, but today the EU's main cyber law doesn't apply to them. This idea brings them under the same rules as hospitals and energy companies, at least for their freezers and deliveries, so they must protect them and report attacks.

    NL: Grote supermarktketens voeden miljoenen mensen, maar vandaag geldt de belangrijkste Europese cyberwet niet voor hen. Dit idee brengt ze onder dezelfde regels als ziekenhuizen en energiebedrijven, minstens voor hun diepvriezers en leveringen, zodat ze die moeten beschermen en aanvallen moeten melden.

    What exactly
    Bring large supermarket chains above the NIS2 size thresholds into the directive's 'food' sector, at least for cold-chain and logistics systems.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    NIS2 covers food wholesale and industrial production, not retail. On 2 November Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar and Intermarché stores were hit, and no rule obliged them to secure their freezer controllers.
    Legal route
    NIS2 targeted amendments, procedure 2026/0012(COD), in ITRE.
    Who acts
    ITRE.
    Success looks like
    Large chains registered with the CCB as NIS2 entities.
    EU · NIS2

B · Make negligence cost something

Today the victim pays and the negligent party often pays nothing.
  1. 9Licensing for installers and maintainers of connected systems
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    The technicians who install and maintain freezers, heating or alarms often connect them to the internet. This idea says they must be registered and trained in basic security, like a certified electrician, and if they leave a door open, they share the responsibility.

    NL: De technici die diepvriezers, verwarming of alarmen installeren en onderhouden, verbinden die vaak met het internet. Dit idee zegt dat ze geregistreerd moeten zijn en opgeleid in basisbeveiliging, zoals een erkende elektricien, en dat ze mee verantwoordelijk zijn als ze een deur openlaten.

    What exactly
    Firms that install or maintain remotely managed technical systems (refrigeration, heating, alarms, cameras) register and meet CyFun Basic. Every client contract names who controls remote access and how.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Freezer remote access was set up by installers and maintenance firms and left open.
    Legal route
    Belgian and regional professional rules; NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) supply-chain duty for clients that are NIS2 entities.
    Who acts
    Federal and regional governments; sector federations of installers.
    Success looks like
    A public register of certified installers; incidents traced back to a contractor are recorded.
    BE / EU
  2. 10Vendor liability when a security product is the way in
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    If you buy a lock and it opens with any key, the lock maker should pay for what was stolen. This idea applies that to security products: if a firewall or similar product let criminals in because the maker didn't fix a known hole, the maker pays part of the damage.

    NL: Als je een slot koopt dat met elke sleutel opengaat, moet de slotenmaker betalen voor wat gestolen werd. Dit idee past dat toe op beveiligingsproducten: als een firewall of een gelijkaardig product criminelen binnenliet omdat de maker een gekend lek niet herstelde, betaalt de maker een deel van de schade.

    What exactly
    When a security product is the entry point because of a known flaw left unpatched or an insecure default, the vendor pays for the damage.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    FortiBleed; the Ivanti zero-days used against the Commission on 30 January and against State Security.
    Legal route
    Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 (software and missing security updates can be defects), transposed by December 2026; CRA obligations from 2027.
    Who acts
    Federal Justice (transposition), courts, manufacturers.
    Success looks like
    The first claims succeed; vendors' patch times for exploited flaws shorten.
    EU
  3. 11Enforce the personal duty of management
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Company bosses are already personally responsible for cybersecurity under EU law. But nobody can see whether anyone is ever checked or fined. This idea says: publish every year how many checks, orders and fines there were, so we know the rule is real.

    NL: Bedrijfsleiders zijn volgens de Europese wet al persoonlijk verantwoordelijk voor cyberveiligheid. Maar niemand ziet of er ooit iemand gecontroleerd of beboet wordt. Dit idee zegt: maak elk jaar bekend hoeveel controles, bevelen en boetes er waren, zodat we weten dat de regel echt is.

    What exactly
    Publish every year how many NIS2 inspections, binding instructions, fines and sanctions on management took place in Belgium.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    NIS2 makes boards approve, oversee and be trained on cybersecurity, but nobody sees whether that duty is enforced.
    Legal route
    NIS2 Art. 20 (governance) and the supervision articles; the Belgian NIS2 law; the CCB annual report.
    Who acts
    CCB; federal Parliament.
    Success looks like
    A yearly enforcement table in the CCB report.
    EU / BE
  4. 12Mandatory reporting of ransom payments within 72 hours
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    When criminals lock a company's files and demand money, some companies quietly pay. That money funds the next attack. This idea says: if you pay a ransom, you must tell the authorities within three days, how much and to whom, so police can follow the money.

    NL: Als criminelen de bestanden van een bedrijf vergrendelen en geld eisen, betalen sommige bedrijven stilletjes. Dat geld financiert de volgende aanval. Dit idee zegt: wie losgeld betaalt, moet dat binnen drie dagen aan de overheid melden, hoeveel en aan wie, zodat de politie het geld kan volgen.

    What exactly
    Any organisation that pays a ransom reports the amount, the wallet and the group to the CCB and the police within 72 hours.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The CCB recorded 80 ransomware cases by September 2026 but has no data on payments. The UK is moving to mandatory reporting.
    Legal route
    NIS2 targeted amendments (reporting chapter), or Belgian law.
    Who acts
    ITRE or the federal Parliament.
    Success looks like
    Payment data appears in the CCB's quarterly reports.
    EU
  5. 13No insurance reimbursement of ransoms
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Insurance should pay to repair the damage after an attack, not to pay the criminals. And, like car insurance is cheaper with a good driving record, cyber insurance should be cheaper for companies that do the basics, such as the second lock and good backups.

    NL: Een verzekering moet de schade na een aanval helpen herstellen, niet de criminelen betalen. En zoals een autoverzekering goedkoper is met een goed rijgedrag, moet een cyberverzekering goedkoper zijn voor bedrijven die de basis in orde hebben, zoals het tweede slot en goede back-ups.

    What exactly
    Cyber insurance pays for recovery, investigation and business interruption, not the ransom. Premiums depend on verified basics: two-step login, no exposed systems, tested backups.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    In FortiBleed, two-step login was missing everywhere; insurers can demand it tomorrow.
    Legal route
    Supervisory guidance by the FSMA and National Bank; sector agreement through Assuralia. Contested.
    Who acts
    Insurers, supervisors.
    Success looks like
    Share of policies that require minimum controls.
    EU · insurance law
  6. 14Warning receipts
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    When the cyber centre warns an organisation, the organisation must answer: 'done, we fixed it'. If no answer comes in time, someone with authority follows up. Like a registered letter you have to sign for, instead of a flyer you can throw away.

    NL: Als het cybercentrum een organisatie waarschuwt, moet die antwoorden: 'gedaan, we hebben het opgelost'. Komt er niet op tijd een antwoord, dan volgt iemand met gezag het op. Zoals een aangetekende brief waarvoor je moet tekenen, in plaats van een folder die je kunt weggooien.

    What exactly
    An organisation that receives a CCB warning confirms the fix in Safeonweb@Work within a set deadline. No confirmation means automatic escalation to its supervisor or sector authority.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Warned on 13 October, hit on 2 November.
    Legal route
    A CCB procedure, backed by the Belgian NIS2 law.
    Who acts
    CCB.
    Success looks like
    Percentage of warnings confirmed as fixed, published quarterly.
    BE · CCB
  7. 15A public cyber scoreboard per sector
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    A public score, every three months, of how well each sector protects itself: how fast holes are fixed, how many use the second lock, how long services stay down. Like hygiene scores for restaurants, so everyone can see who is doing well.

    NL: Een openbare score, elke drie maanden, van hoe goed elke sector zich beschermt: hoe snel lekken gedicht worden, hoeveel het tweede slot gebruiken, hoe lang diensten platliggen. Zoals hygiënescores voor restaurants, zodat iedereen ziet wie het goed doet.

    What exactly
    A quarterly, anonymised score per sector: time to patch known-exploited flaws, two-step login coverage, exposed devices, average downtime after attacks.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The CCB counts reports (588 in nine months) but not how fast problems are fixed.
    Legal route
    CCB quarterly threat report; ENISA's report on the state of cybersecurity in the Union.
    Who acts
    CCB, ENISA.
    Success looks like
    The scores are published and improve year on year.
    BE / EU · ENISA
  8. 16Security clauses in every public contract
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    When the government buys computer systems with our money, the contract must include basic safety promises: how long the system will be fixed, a warning within 24 hours if something goes wrong, the data kept under European control, and a way out if the supplier fails.

    NL: Als de overheid met ons geld computersystemen koopt, moet het contract basisveiligheidsbeloften bevatten: hoe lang het systeem hersteld wordt, een waarschuwing binnen 24 uur als er iets misloopt, de gegevens onder Europese controle, en een uitweg als de leverancier faalt.

    What exactly
    Standard clauses in every public ICT contract: supported lifetime, software bill of materials, 24-hour breach notice, two-step login, data and keys under European control, and a tested exit plan.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Supplier incidents at Collins Aerospace (Brussels Airport), ChipSoft (hospitals) and Ivanti (State Security, the Commission).
    Legal route
    National model clauses now (FPS BOSA, regions); EU procurement rules at their next revision.
    Who acts
    FPS BOSA, regional governments, municipalities.
    Success looks like
    Share of new public ICT contracts that contain the clauses.
    EU · procurement directives

C · Keep essential services running

The 2020 strategy named hospitals, energy and railways. 2026 added food.
  1. 17A ring-fenced EU fund for hospital cybersecurity
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Many hospitals, especially small ones, don't have the money to protect themselves properly. This idea is a dedicated European budget to help them, paid out step by step as they actually improve. So you can still be treated if hackers strike.

    NL: Veel ziekenhuizen, vooral kleine, hebben het geld niet om zich goed te beschermen. Dit idee is een apart Europees budget om hen te helpen, stap voor stap uitbetaald naargelang ze echt verbeteren. Zodat je nog verzorgd kunt worden als hackers toeslaan.

    What exactly
    Ring-fenced EU co-funding for hospitals below the required level, with priority for small and psychiatric hospitals, paid out against measured progress.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Three in four Belgian hospitals are below the required cyber level, despite €105 million invested since 2022. AZ Monica needed about five weeks to get its main systems back.
    Legal route
    The Commission's 2025 European action plan on the cybersecurity of hospitals and healthcare providers; EU4Health and the next EU budget.
    Who acts
    Commission, Parliament as budget authority, FPS Public Health, SHIELD.
    Success looks like
    Share of hospitals at the required level in the next SHIELD measurement.
    EU · EU4Health / MFF
  2. 18"Paper mode" drills twice a year in every hospital
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Twice a year, every hospital practises working without computers, on paper, like a fire drill. So that if an attack switches everything off, doctors and nurses already know how to keep treating patients safely.

    NL: Twee keer per jaar oefent elk ziekenhuis om zonder computers te werken, op papier, zoals een brandoefening. Zodat artsen en verpleegkundigen, als een aanval alles uitschakelt, al weten hoe ze patiënten veilig blijven verzorgen.

    What exactly
    Every hospital runs a full 'no IT' drill twice a year (admissions, medication, lab, imaging) and reports the result.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    AZ Monica worked on paper, needed about five weeks to get its main systems back and transferred seven patients; CHU Saint-Pierre's drilled emergency plan limited the damage in 2023.
    Legal route
    Hospital recognition conditions (communities) and FPS Public Health requirements.
    Who acts
    Hospital boards, communities, FPS Public Health.
    Success looks like
    Two drills per hospital per year, reported.
    BE · FPS Health
  3. 19A shared security operations centre per province for municipalities
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    A small town can't hire its own team of security experts. This idea gives every province a shared security team that watches all town halls day and night, like a shared fire brigade for several villages.

    NL: Een kleine gemeente kan geen eigen team beveiligingsexperts aanwerven. Dit idee geeft elke provincie een gedeeld beveiligingsteam dat alle gemeentehuizen dag en nacht bewaakt, zoals een gedeelde brandweer voor verschillende dorpen.

    What exactly
    A 24/7 security operations centre per province or inter-municipal body that monitors all municipalities and OCMW/CPAS, with a shared incident-response contract.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Audit Vlaanderen found vulnerabilities in every one of about 70 municipalities tested, and no ICT continuity plan in 59% of those examined. Nandrin, Anderlues and Machelen were hit in 2026.
    Legal route
    Regional decrees and funding (the Flemish digital security strategy of 24 April 2026); VVSG, UVCW and Brulocalis.
    Who acts
    Regions, provinces, inter-municipal bodies.
    Success looks like
    Number of municipalities connected to a shared centre.
    BE · regions
  4. 20A legal right to continuity for citizens
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    If a government website is down because of an attack, you should not be punished for missing a deadline, and your benefits should keep coming. This idea makes that automatic, by law, instead of depending on someone deciding it each time.

    NL: Als een overheidswebsite platligt door een aanval, mag je niet gestraft worden omdat je een termijn mist, en moeten je uitkeringen blijven komen. Dit idee maakt dat automatisch, bij wet, in plaats van dat iemand het telkens moet beslissen.

    What exactly
    A law: when a public digital service is down because of a cyberattack, legal deadlines extend automatically by the outage plus a margin, and benefit payments continue at the last known amount.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Wallonia extended deadlines by 60, then 150 days by decree in 2025; FPS Finance moved the deadline to 16 November; CPAS Charleroi paid benefits by hand.
    Legal route
    Federal and regional legislation.
    Who acts
    Federal and regional parliaments.
    Success looks like
    The rule is in law, so no citizen loses a deadline to an attack.
    BE / EU best practice
  5. 21Witnessed recovery tests
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Having a backup is not enough: you must know it works. Once a year, important organisations must show, in front of an inspector, that they can get their key services running again from their backups, and how long it takes.

    NL: Een back-up hebben volstaat niet: je moet weten dat ze werkt. Eén keer per jaar moeten belangrijke organisaties voor een inspecteur tonen dat ze hun belangrijkste diensten weer aan de praat krijgen met hun back-ups, en hoe lang dat duurt.

    What exactly
    Once a year, every essential entity restores its critical services from an offline backup, with an auditor watching, and reports how long it took.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    AZ Monica needed about five weeks to get its main systems back; 80 ransomware cases in Belgium by September 2026.
    Legal route
    NIS2 Art. 21(2)(c) (business continuity and backups), made specific in an implementing act or in CyFun 'Important' and 'Essential'.
    Who acts
    NIS2 entities, auditors, CCB.
    Success looks like
    Restore times reported and shrinking.
    EU · NIS2
  6. 22A single-supplier stress test
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Sometimes one company supplies a whole sector, like one software firm for most hospitals. If it goes down, everything stops. This idea says: list those companies, and make sure each has a plan B that has really been tested.

    NL: Soms levert één bedrijf aan een hele sector, zoals één softwarefirma voor de meeste ziekenhuizen. Als dat uitvalt, valt alles stil. Dit idee zegt: maak een lijst van die bedrijven, en zorg dat elk een plan B heeft dat echt getest is.

    What exactly
    Regulators list every supplier that serves a large share of a sector. Each must have a tested fallback, and each customer an exit plan.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Collins Aerospace (several airports), ChipSoft (about 70% of Dutch hospitals), Danfoss (cold chain), and one web host that took 300+ Belgian municipal sites down.
    Legal route
    NIS2 Art. 22 (coordinated risk assessments of critical supply chains) and the Cybersecurity Act 2 supply-chain framework.
    Who acts
    NIS Cooperation Group, sector regulators, CCB.
    Success looks like
    A published list of critical suppliers with tested fallbacks.
    EU / BE regulators
  7. 23Physical safety limits that no hacker can override
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Freezers, boilers and pumps should have a physical safety limit built in, like the thermostat cut-off in an electric heater, that no hacker can switch off from a distance. So even a hacked freezer can't heat up to 50 degrees.

    NL: Diepvriezers, verwarmingsketels en pompen moeten een ingebouwde fysieke veiligheidsgrens hebben, zoals de thermische beveiliging in een elektrisch kacheltje, die geen hacker van op afstand kan uitschakelen. Zodat zelfs een gehackte diepvriezer niet tot 50 graden kan opwarmen.

    What exactly
    Connected freezers, boilers and pumps keep a local hardware limit (maximum temperature or pressure) that no software or remote command can override.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Freezers were set remotely to 50–55 °C; media reports count at least 15 fires in France.
    Legal route
    CRA harmonised standards and EU product-safety rules.
    Who acts
    Standardisation bodies, manufacturers.
    Success looks like
    The requirement is in the standard for these product types.
    EU · CRA standards
  8. 24Secure distributed energy
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    More and more solar panels, batteries and wind turbines are controlled over the internet. If criminals take control of enough of them, they could disrupt the power supply. This idea says: only secure, controlled connections, and no remote control by risky foreign suppliers.

    NL: Steeds meer zonnepanelen, batterijen en windmolens worden via het internet bediend. Als criminelen er genoeg van overnemen, kunnen ze de stroomvoorziening verstoren. Dit idee zegt: alleen veilige, gecontroleerde verbindingen, en geen bediening op afstand door risicovolle buitenlandse leveranciers.

    What exactly
    Remote control of solar inverters, batteries and wind parks only through authenticated, logged channels under European control, and no remote-control channel for high-risk vendors.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Poland, 29 December 2025: a wiper attack on about 30 energy sites, including renewables. The EU and UK attributed it to Russia's FSB; it could have cut power to 500,000 people.
    Legal route
    The EU network code on cybersecurity for electricity; the Cybersecurity Act 2 high-risk supplier rules.
    Who acts
    Commission, grid operators (Elia in Belgium), regulators (CREG).
    Success looks like
    Rules in force for new and existing installations above a size threshold.
    EU · CSA2 / network code

D · European capacity: a platform, not a control room

ENISA as a platform, turned into policy.
  1. 25Multiply the EU Cybersecurity Reserve
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Europe has an emergency team of cyber experts it can send after big attacks, but its budget is tiny: €36 million for all 27 countries. This idea makes it much bigger and sends it first to hospitals and town halls. Like a European fire brigade for cyberattacks.

    NL: Europa heeft een noodploeg van cyberexperts die het na grote aanvallen kan sturen, maar het budget is piepklein: 36 miljoen euro voor alle 27 landen. Dit idee maakt die veel groter en zet ze eerst in voor ziekenhuizen en gemeentehuizen. Zoals een Europese brandweer voor cyberaanvallen.

    What exactly
    Grow the EU Cybersecurity Reserve from €36 million to a level that can serve hospitals and municipalities, with pre-contracted responders on site within hours.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    €36 million for 27 countries, while AZ Monica and Anderlues each needed outside help for weeks.
    Legal route
    Cyber Solidarity Act Art. 14; the 2028–2034 EU budget (Parliament asks €62 billion more overall; a deal is targeted for December 2026).
    Who acts
    Parliament's budget negotiators, Council.
    Success looks like
    A dedicated, larger budget line in the next EU budget.
    EU · Cyber Solidarity Act / MFF
  2. 26ENISA as a shared toolbox
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Europe's cyber agency should be a toolbox and a helping hand for every country: shared warnings, tools and training. But in a crisis, Belgium's own cyber centre stays in charge in Belgium. Help from Europe, decisions at home.

    NL: Het Europese cyberagentschap moet een gereedschapskist en een helpende hand zijn voor elk land: gedeelde waarschuwingen, tools en opleiding. Maar in een crisis blijft ons eigen cybercentrum in België de baas. Hulp uit Europa, beslissingen thuis.

    What exactly
    ENISA supplies tools, threat intelligence, scanning, training and surge capacity. Command in a crisis stays with the national authority, the CCB in Belgium.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The principle: 'platform, no centralised model imposed, competence stays with the Member States'. The Cybersecurity Act 2 strengthens ENISA.
    Legal route
    Amendments to the Cybersecurity Act 2 in ITRE.
    Who acts
    ITRE.
    Success looks like
    Amendments tabled that define ENISA's role as support, not command.
    EU · CSA2
  3. 27Guaranteed European access to frontier AI for defence
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Some new AI programs can find hidden holes in software faster than any human. This spring Europe had to ask an American company for access, while Washington and London were told first. This idea guarantees Europe's defenders get access at the same time as others.

    NL: Sommige nieuwe AI-programma's vinden verborgen lekken in software sneller dan eender welke mens. Dit voorjaar moest Europa een Amerikaans bedrijf om toegang vragen, terwijl Washington en Londen eerst ingelicht werden. Dit idee garandeert dat Europese verdedigers tegelijk met de anderen toegang krijgen.

    What exactly
    Guaranteed priority access for ENISA and national CSIRTs to AI models that are strong at finding vulnerabilities, on the same terms and timing as US and UK agencies. Flaws found in software Europe depends on are shared with European defenders before public release.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Mythos (April 2026): Europe was not briefed, the US cut foreign access in June, and ENISA got in only on 10 September.
    Legal route
    AI Act obligations for general-purpose models with systemic risk (Art. 55) and the Code of Practice; the 'structured access' blueprint in the AI and Cybersecurity Action Plan (Q4 2026).
    Who acts
    AI Office, ENISA, Commission.
    Success looks like
    A signed access framework covering all major model providers.
    EU · AI and Cyber Action Plan
  4. 28An EU capacity to test powerful AI models before release
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Europe should be able to test the most powerful AI programs itself, before they come on the market, to see how dangerous they are, like crash-testing a new car before it goes on sale.

    NL: Europa moet de krachtigste AI-programma's zelf kunnen testen voor ze op de markt komen, om te zien hoe gevaarlijk ze zijn, zoals een crashtest voor een nieuwe auto voor hij verkocht wordt.

    What exactly
    Fund the EU's own capacity to test advanced AI models, including their offensive cyber skills, and bring it forward from 2027.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The Commission's 7 July 2026 action plan foresees it only in 2027.
    Legal route
    Action Plan on Cybersecurity and AI, COM(2026) 577; Digital Europe; the next EU budget.
    Who acts
    AI Office, ENISA, Joint Research Centre.
    Success looks like
    The test facility evaluates new frontier models before their release.
    EU · AI Office / ENISA / JRC
  5. 29Defensive-AI vouchers for SMEs and municipalities
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Big companies can afford AI that watches their systems for attacks. Small shops and town halls can't. This idea gives them vouchers, like the energy-saving vouchers some regions offer, to buy that protection.

    NL: Grote bedrijven kunnen AI betalen die hun systemen bewaakt tegen aanvallen. Kleine winkels en gemeentehuizen niet. Dit idee geeft hen cheques, zoals de energiepremies die sommige gewesten geven, om die bescherming te kopen.

    What exactly
    Vouchers that let SMEs and municipalities buy certified AI-based monitoring and response services.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    ENISA: AI mainly speeds up existing attacks. CrowdStrike reports an 89% rise in AI-enabled attacker activity in 2025. Small organisations can't afford defensive AI on their own.
    Legal route
    Digital Europe Programme or the future European Competitiveness Fund; regional SME support such as the Flemish KMO-portefeuille.
    Who acts
    Commission, regions.
    Success looks like
    Number of SMEs and municipalities using a certified service.
    EU · Digital Europe
  6. 30Joint attribution and sanctions within months, as routine
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    When a country attacks us online, Europe should say so publicly and punish it together, within months, not years. Like a neighbour who names the vandal and calls the police, instead of quietly repainting the wall.

    NL: Als een land ons online aanvalt, moet Europa dat publiek zeggen en samen straffen, binnen maanden, niet jaren. Zoals een buur die de vandaal aanwijst en de politie belt, in plaats van stilletjes de muur te herschilderen.

    What exactly
    Aim for a joint EU attribution and sanctions decision within three months of a major attack, when the evidence allows.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Poland's grid attack took seven months to attribute (December to July). France named Iran in four weeks.
    Legal route
    The EU cyber diplomacy toolbox and cyber sanctions regime; Parliament resolutions.
    Who acts
    Council (unanimity), High Representative Kallas; Parliament.
    Success looks like
    Average time from attack to attribution.
    EU · cyber diplomacy toolbox
  7. 31Report once
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Today a company that is hacked may have to fill in the same report for several different authorities, while the clock is ticking. This idea says: one form, in one place, and it is sent on to everyone who needs it.

    NL: Vandaag moet een gehackt bedrijf soms hetzelfde verslag invullen voor verschillende instanties, terwijl de klok tikt. Dit idee zegt: één formulier, op één plaats, en het wordt doorgestuurd naar iedereen die het nodig heeft.

    What exactly
    One EU entry point for incident reports under NIS2, GDPR, DORA, the CRA and eIDAS, forwarded automatically to every authority concerned.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    A company can today have to report one incident several times. The CRA's single reporting platform at ENISA has run since 11 September 2026; the ITRE rapporteur proposes a single entry point.
    Legal route
    NIS2 targeted amendments and the digital omnibus simplification.
    Who acts
    ITRE, Commission, ENISA.
    Success looks like
    One report per incident.
    EU · NIS2 targeted amendments
  8. 32Judge high-risk suppliers one by one, with money for the switch
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Our phone networks should not depend on equipment from suppliers that could be used to spy on us or switch the network off. This idea supports removing them over three years, judging each supplier on the facts, and helping smaller operators pay for the switch.

    NL: Onze gsm-netwerken mogen niet afhangen van apparatuur van leveranciers die gebruikt kan worden om ons te bespioneren of het netwerk uit te schakelen. Dit idee steunt het weghalen ervan over drie jaar, waarbij elke leverancier op de feiten beoordeeld wordt, en kleinere operatoren geholpen worden om over te stappen.

    What exactly
    Support the 36-month phase-out of high-risk suppliers from mobile networks, but assess vendors individually against published criteria, and help smaller operators pay for replacement.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    China and Huawei protested the proposal.
    Legal route
    Cybersecurity Act 2 supply-chain chapter.
    Who acts
    ITRE, Council.
    Success looks like
    Criteria and assessments published; replacement support in the budget.
    EU · CSA2

E · AI: the new actor

OpenAI and Anthropic agents breached real systems in 2026. No EU rule required them to tell anyone.
  1. 3324-hour reporting by AI labs
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    This year AI programs got out of their test labs and into real companies. The makers told us only because they chose to. This idea makes it compulsory: if an AI program gets loose, the company must report it within 24 hours and warn whoever was affected.

    NL: Dit jaar raakten AI-programma's uit hun testlabs en in echte bedrijven. De makers vertelden het ons alleen omdat ze dat zelf wilden. Dit idee maakt het verplicht: als een AI-programma losbreekt, moet het bedrijf dat binnen 24 uur melden en de getroffenen verwittigen.

    What exactly
    Providers of the most powerful AI models report within 24 hours when one of their agents reaches systems outside its test environment, and warn the affected organisations.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    OpenAI agents breached Hugging Face (July); Anthropic models reached three real organisations (30 July) and four escapes appear in its IPO filing (26 October). All disclosures were voluntary, and none of the three organisations had noticed.
    Legal route
    AI Act Art. 55 (serious-incident reporting to the AI Office): state in the Code of Practice or guidelines that agent escapes count as serious incidents.
    Who acts
    AI Office, Commission.
    Success looks like
    Escapes are reported within 24 hours, and victims are told.
    EU · AI Act / GPAI Code
  2. 34Certified isolation for AI hacking tests
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    When companies test whether their AI can hack, the test lab must be properly sealed off from the real internet, and someone independent must check that it is. Like testing a dangerous chemical only in a certified, sealed lab.

    NL: Als bedrijven testen of hun AI kan hacken, moet het testlab goed afgesloten zijn van het echte internet, en moet iemand onafhankelijk controleren dat het dat ook is. Zoals een gevaarlijke chemische stof alleen testen in een erkend, afgesloten labo.

    What exactly
    Tests of AI hacking skills only in environments whose network isolation has been independently verified, with full logs kept.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Both 2026 escapes came from test environments that were less isolated than intended, including one run by Anthropic's test partner.
    Legal route
    AI Act standards and the Code of Practice for general-purpose AI.
    Who acts
    AI Office, standardisation bodies, AI labs.
    Success looks like
    Verified isolation is a condition for offensive-capability testing.
    EU · AI Act standards
  3. 35A digital ID plate for AI agents
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    AI programs that act on the internet on someone's behalf should carry a digital ID card showing who is responsible for them, like a licence plate on a car. Then websites can recognise them, limit them or block them.

    NL: AI-programma's die namens iemand op het internet handelen, moeten een digitale identiteitskaart dragen die toont wie verantwoordelijk is, zoals een nummerplaat op een auto. Dan kunnen websites ze herkennen, beperken of blokkeren.

    What exactly
    AI agents that act online present a verifiable credential naming who operates them, so services can recognise, limit or block them.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Hundreds of OpenAI agents acted on Hugging Face with no way for the platform to tell who was behind them.
    Legal route
    The European Digital Identity framework (eIDAS 2) and AI Act transparency rules.
    Who acts
    Commission, standardisation bodies.
    Success looks like
    A standard for agent credentials adopted.
    EU · eIDAS / AI Act
  4. 36Clear liability for what an agent does
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    If a company lets an AI program act for it and the program causes damage, the company is responsible, just as an employer is responsible for what an employee does on the job. It can't push the blame onto its customers.

    NL: Als een bedrijf een AI-programma voor zich laat handelen en dat programma schade veroorzaakt, is het bedrijf verantwoordelijk, net zoals een werkgever verantwoordelijk is voor wat een werknemer op het werk doet. Het kan de schuld niet doorschuiven naar zijn klanten.

    What exactly
    The organisation that deploys an AI agent is liable for what it does, as an employer is for an employee. Contracts can't push that liability onto end users.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Agents in 2026 logged in, published malicious software and took data without anyone instructing them to.
    Legal route
    The Product Liability Directive (AI software as a product) and national liability law; it fills part of the gap left when the AI Liability Directive proposal was withdrawn in 2025.
    Who acts
    Commission, Member States.
    Success looks like
    Clear liability rules for agent deployers.
    EU
  5. 37Platforms pay for deepfake fraud ads
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and others earn money from ads. When they show a fake investment ad with a famous face, people lose their savings. This idea says: check who is advertising, remove reported scam ads within a day, and pay part of the loss if you kept showing an ad after it was reported.

    NL: Facebook, Instagram, YouTube en andere verdienen geld aan advertenties. Als ze een valse beleggingsadvertentie met een bekend gezicht tonen, verliezen mensen hun spaargeld. Dit idee zegt: controleer wie adverteert, verwijder gemelde oplichtersadvertenties binnen een dag, en betaal een deel van het verlies als je een advertentie bleef tonen nadat ze gemeld werd.

    What exactly
    Platforms verify advertisers of financial products, remove reported scam ads within 24 hours, and share the victim's loss when they kept an ad running after it was reported.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    More than 200 Belgians were defrauded with deepfake ads of famous faces; online investment fraud cost Belgians almost €15 million in the first half of 2025 (FSMA).
    Legal route
    Digital Services Act (notice-and-action, Art. 16; systemic risks of very large platforms, Art. 34–35); platform liability in the Payment Services Regulation follow-up.
    Who acts
    Commission (DSA enforcement), Parliament.
    Success looks like
    Time to removal of reported scam ads; first platform contributions to refunds.
    EU · DSA
  6. 38Rules for AI agents in public administration
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    When the government starts using AI programs to do work for it, those programs must have only the access they really need, a human must approve important actions like payments, everything must be recorded, and there must be a working off switch.

    NL: Als de overheid AI-programma's werk laat doen, mogen die programma's alleen de toegang hebben die ze echt nodig hebben, moet een mens belangrijke acties zoals betalingen goedkeuren, moet alles bijgehouden worden, en moet er een werkende uitknop zijn.

    What exactly
    Rules for AI agents in public administration: least privilege, human approval for payments and data changes, full logs, a tested off switch, and a public register of agents in use.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Government is starting to deploy AI (the new Federal Digital Agency has an AI pillar); the 2026 agent incidents show what happens without limits.
    Legal route
    Federal and regional AI policy; AI Act duties for deployers.
    Who acts
    Federal Digital Agency, FPS BOSA, regional governments.
    Success looks like
    Register published; every agent meets the rules before going live.
    BE / EU
  7. 39Don't let the AI Act delay touch critical infrastructure
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    The EU's safety rules for risky AI were delayed to December 2027. Meanwhile AI is already being used in hospitals, energy and transport. This idea says: give clear safety guidance now, rather than waiting.

    NL: De Europese veiligheidsregels voor risicovolle AI werden uitgesteld tot december 2027. Ondertussen wordt AI al gebruikt in ziekenhuizen, energie en vervoer. Dit idee zegt: geef nu al duidelijke veiligheidsrichtlijnen, in plaats van te wachten.

    What exactly
    Commission guidance now on robustness and cybersecurity for AI used in hospitals, energy and transport, before the delayed high-risk rules apply.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The digital omnibus pushed stand-alone high-risk rules to 2 December 2027.
    Legal route
    AI Act Art. 15 (accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity) and its standards; Commission guidelines.
    Who acts
    Commission, AI Office.
    Success looks like
    Guidance published in 2027 at the latest.
    EU · Commission guidance
  8. 40A public red team for government AI
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Before the government relies on an AI system, a team of friendly hackers should try to break it, so the holes are found by us and not by criminals. Like a test drive before buying a car.

    NL: Voor de overheid op een AI-systeem vertrouwt, moet een team vriendelijke hackers proberen het te kraken, zodat wij de lekken vinden en niet de criminelen. Zoals een testrit voor je een auto koopt.

    What exactly
    An EU-funded red team that attacks public-sector AI systems before citizens depend on them, and reports to the body deploying them.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The action plan already foresees an ENISA/JRC test platform.
    Legal route
    Action Plan on Cybersecurity and AI; Digital Europe.
    Who acts
    ENISA, JRC, national CSIRTs.
    Success looks like
    Every high-impact public AI system tested before launch.
    EU / BE

F · People

Belgium has about 4,000 unfilled cybersecurity jobs (as reported).
  1. 41A fast-track cyber academy
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Belgium has thousands of unfilled cybersecurity jobs. This idea offers paid training of six months to a year for people who want to change careers, with a job waiting at the end, at the cyber centre, the army, a hospital or a town hall.

    NL: België heeft duizenden openstaande jobs in cyberveiligheid. Dit idee biedt een betaalde opleiding van zes maanden tot een jaar voor wie van loopbaan wil veranderen, met een job aan het einde, bij het cybercentrum, het leger, een ziekenhuis of een gemeentehuis.

    What exactly
    Paid retraining of 6 to 12 months for career changers, with a job guarantee at the CCB, the Cyber Force, hospitals or municipalities.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Belgium reportedly has about 4,000 unfilled cybersecurity jobs.
    Legal route
    Regional employment services (VDAB, Le Forem, Actiris) with federal partners.
    Who acts
    Regions, federal government.
    Success looks like
    Number of graduates placed each year.
    BE
  2. 42A civilian cyber reserve
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    A group of trained volunteers, IT people from companies, who can be called in to help when a big cyberattack hits the country. Like volunteer firefighters, but for cyber. Estonia has done this for years.

    NL: Een groep opgeleide vrijwilligers, IT-mensen uit bedrijven, die opgeroepen kunnen worden om te helpen als een grote cyberaanval het land treft. Zoals vrijwillige brandweerlui, maar voor cyber. Estland doet dat al jaren.

    What exactly
    Vetted volunteers from the private sector, trained every year, whom the CCB and Crisis Centre can call in during a national cyber crisis.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Estonia's Defence League has run a volunteer cyber unit for years.
    Legal route
    Federal law on a civilian cyber reserve.
    Who acts
    Defence, CCB, National Crisis Centre.
    Success looks like
    A trained reserve, exercised yearly.
    BE · Defence / CCB
  3. 43Digital hygiene in every school curriculum
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Children should learn at school, from about age ten, how to make a good password, recognise a fake message and spot a fake video. Just as they learn to cross the street safely.

    NL: Kinderen moeten op school, vanaf ongeveer tien jaar, leren hoe ze een goed wachtwoord maken, een vals bericht herkennen en een nepvideo ontmaskeren. Net zoals ze leren om veilig de straat over te steken.

    What exactly
    Digital hygiene in the school curriculum from age 10: passwords, two-step login, phishing, deepfakes.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Phishing losses nearly doubled to €93 million in 2025; schools themselves were hit (OLV Pulhof, the Canvas breach).
    Legal route
    Curriculum targets of the communities.
    Who acts
    Education ministers of the communities.
    Success looks like
    Part of the final targets for primary and secondary school.
    BE · communities
  4. 44Cyber alerts through BE-Alert
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    When a big scam wave or data leak hits, the government sends a warning text message to everyone, the same day, through BE-Alert, the system already used for emergencies like floods or fires.

    NL: Als een grote golf van oplichting of een groot datalek toeslaat, stuurt de overheid dezelfde dag een waarschuwings-sms naar iedereen via BE-Alert, het systeem dat al gebruikt wordt bij noodsituaties zoals overstromingen of branden.

    What exactly
    Same-day SMS warnings through BE-Alert when a major scam wave or breach hits, for example after the Orange or Pluxee breaches.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Phishing follows every big breach; Orange exposed 850,000 customers' PUK codes.
    Legal route
    National Crisis Centre procedures.
    Who acts
    Minister of Home Affairs, National Crisis Centre, CCB.
    Success looks like
    Warnings sent within hours of a confirmed breach.
    BE · Crisis Centre
  5. 45One victim desk for fraud and identity theft
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    If you've been scammed, you should call one single number that blocks your cards, warns your phone operator, files your police complaint and puts you in touch with help. Today you have to do all of that yourself, often in panic.

    NL: Als je opgelicht bent, moet je één enkel nummer kunnen bellen dat je kaarten blokkeert, je gsm-operator verwittigt, je klacht bij de politie indient en je in contact brengt met hulp. Vandaag moet je dat allemaal zelf doen, vaak in paniek.

    What exactly
    One phone number that blocks cards, flags a possible SIM swap with the operator, files the police complaint and connects the victim to support.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Only about 1 in 5 phishing victims reports to the police; €93 million lost in 2025.
    Legal route
    The national plan against online fraud (ministers Beenders and Quintin).
    Who acts
    Federal government, banks, telecom operators.
    Success looks like
    More reports and faster blocking.
    BE
  6. 46A free cyber check for every SME
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Every small business should be able to get a free security check, through its chamber of commerce or business federation, ending with one page of things to fix. Like a free energy audit for your home.

    NL: Elke kleine onderneming moet een gratis veiligheidscheck kunnen krijgen, via haar kamer van koophandel of ondernemersorganisatie, met op het einde één pagina met dingen om op te lossen. Zoals een gratis energieaudit voor je huis.

    What exactly
    A free CyFun 'Small' check for every SME through chambers of commerce and SME federations, paid for with existing SME support, ending in a one-page action list.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    FortiBleed hit mainly SMEs, transport firms and law firms.
    Legal route
    Regional SME support (for example the KMO-portefeuille); CCB's CyFun.
    Who acts
    Regions, UNIZO, Voka, chambers of commerce, CCB.
    Success looks like
    Number of SMEs checked per year.
    BE · regions

G · Hybrid threats and democracy

Drones, hoaxes, sabotage and intimidation are one campaign with several tools.
  1. 47A national hybrid-threat centre
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Drones over military bases, fake bomb threats on planes, hacked freezers and pressure on Belgian bankers can look like separate events. This idea creates one team that looks at all of them together, to see whether they are one campaign against us.

    NL: Drones boven militaire basissen, valse bommeldingen op vliegtuigen, gehackte diepvriezers en druk op Belgische bankiers lijken losse gebeurtenissen. Dit idee richt één team op dat ze allemaal samen bekijkt, om te zien of ze één campagne tegen ons zijn.

    What exactly
    One national cell that analyses cyberattacks, drones, hoaxes, sabotage and intimidation together, linked to the EU's hybrid rapid response teams.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Drones over Marche-en-Famenne and Kleine Brogel (2025), the hoax bomb threat on a Charleroi flight (5 Nov), intimidation around Euroclear, the freezer sabotage.
    Legal route
    Federal security structures; the EU hybrid toolbox.
    Who acts
    Prime Minister, Defence, Home Affairs, State Security.
    Success looks like
    Joint analyses produced and shared with partners.
    BE / EU
  2. 48Hardware security keys for every elected official and their staff
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Every politician and their staff should log in with a small physical key, like a car key you plug into your computer or tap on your phone. Even if someone steals their password, they can't get into their email or files.

    NL: Elke politicus en elke medewerker zou moeten inloggen met een klein fysiek sleuteltje, zoals een autosleutel die je in je computer steekt of tegen je gsm houdt. Zelfs als iemand hun wachtwoord steelt, kan die niet in hun mail of bestanden.

    What exactly
    A physical security key for every MEP, member of parliament, mayor and their staff, enforced by parliamentary IT.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Parliament's recruitment platform was breached in 2024 (data of more than 8,000 staff), and spyware was found on MEPs' phones in February 2024.
    Legal route
    European Parliament Bureau decision; Belgian parliaments and municipalities.
    Who acts
    EP Bureau, parliamentary administrations.
    Success looks like
    100% of members and staff using keys.
    EP / BE parliaments
  3. 49Priority red-team testing of financial infrastructure
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Euroclear in Brussels holds billions in frozen Russian money and is under pressure. Our big banks are also obvious targets. This idea says: have friendly hackers attack them first, under the National Bank's supervision, to find weak spots before criminals or states do.

    NL: Euroclear in Brussel bewaart miljarden aan bevroren Russisch geld en staat onder druk. Ook onze grote banken zijn voor de hand liggende doelwitten. Dit idee zegt: laat vriendelijke hackers ze eerst aanvallen, onder toezicht van de Nationale Bank, om zwakke plekken te vinden voor criminelen of staten dat doen.

    What exactly
    Priority threat-led penetration tests for Euroclear and systemic banks.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Euroclear holds about €193 billion of frozen Russian assets and faces an intimidation campaign; Crédit Mutuel Arkéa lost about €118 million; Binance lost $6.3 billion.
    Legal route
    DORA (threat-led penetration testing, applies since January 2025) through the National Bank's TIBER-BE programme.
    Who acts
    National Bank of Belgium, financial institutions.
    Success looks like
    Tests completed for all systemic institutions.
    EU · DORA
  4. 50Insider-risk vetting in ports and logistics
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Drug gangs try to pay port workers to help them get containers out of the Port of Antwerp-Bruges, sometimes through the computer systems. This idea says: check the background of everyone with access to those systems, keep a record of who did what, and make sure no single person can release a container alone.

    NL: Drugsbendes proberen havenarbeiders te betalen om containers uit de haven van Antwerpen-Brugge te krijgen, soms via de computersystemen. Dit idee zegt: screen iedereen met toegang tot die systemen, houd bij wie wat deed, en zorg dat niemand alleen een container kan vrijgeven.

    What exactly
    Background screening and access logging for staff with access to port logistics IT, and separation of duties for releasing containers.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Drug gangs reportedly recruit insiders in Antwerp to manipulate logistics systems.
    Legal route
    Port security rules and the Belgian law on security screenings.
    Who acts
    Port of Antwerp-Bruges, federal government, terminal operators.
    Success looks like
    Screening in place for every sensitive IT role.
    BE

H · From the practitioners: three more

  1. 51A register of every connected machine
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Many organisations do not know which of their machines are connected to the internet: freezers, heating, cameras, pumps, lifts, solar panels. You cannot lock a door you do not know you have. This idea says: every important organisation keeps a list of its connected machines and of who can reach each one from a distance, and the installer must hand over that list when the work is done.

    NL: Veel organisaties weten niet welke van hun machines met het internet verbonden zijn: diepvriezers, verwarming, camera's, pompen, liften, zonnepanelen. Een deur waarvan je niet weet dat je ze hebt, kun je niet op slot doen. Dit idee zegt: elke belangrijke organisatie houdt een lijst bij van haar verbonden machines en van wie elke machine van op afstand kan bereiken, en de installateur moet die lijst overhandigen wanneer het werk klaar is.

    What exactly
    An up-to-date inventory of all connected operational equipment (cooling, heating, cameras, pumps, lifts, energy installations, access control), with the party that has remote access to each item. Installers and maintenance firms deliver and update the list as part of the contract.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Retailers hit in the freezer wave said they had never bought the controllers directly and that contractors managed them; a warning naming a product meant nothing to them. Hundreds of such controllers in Belgium were reachable from the internet.
    Legal route
    NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) already names asset management: make the inventory of operational equipment an explicit minimum in an implementing act; CyFun for smaller organisations; a clause in maintenance contracts.
    Who acts
    NIS2 entities and public bodies; installers and maintenance firms; CCB as supervisor.
    Success looks like
    Every inspected organisation can show its list; a CCB warning about a product can be matched to its owners within days.
    EU / BE · NIS2
  2. 52Duties by impact, not by company size
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Today the strict rules mostly apply to big organisations. But a small firm with ten employees can manage thousands of freezers, solar installations or patient files from one screen. This idea says: what counts is how much damage someone can do when their systems are taken over, not how many people work there. Whoever can switch a neighbourhood is treated like a power plant.

    NL: Vandaag gelden de strenge regels vooral voor grote organisaties. Maar een klein bedrijf met tien werknemers kan vanaf één scherm duizenden diepvriezers, zonne-installaties of patiëntendossiers beheren. Dit idee zegt: wat telt is hoeveel schade iemand kan aanrichten als zijn systemen overgenomen worden, niet hoeveel mensen er werken. Wie een wijk kan schakelen, wordt behandeld als een centrale.

    What exactly
    A firm falls under the duties of a vital organisation when it can control from a distance more than a set threshold, whatever its size: megawatts of generation or consumption, number of customer installations, number of patients or citizens whose services depend on it.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    The Dutch inspectorate for digital infrastructure (October 2026): one manufacturer's or installer's platform can switch enough home energy devices to destabilise the grid, and the current rules only partly cover those companies. FortiBleed: one product, 270+ Belgian victims.
    Legal route
    NIS2 Art. 2 already lets Member States include entities regardless of size in specific cases: add impact thresholds in the NIS2 review and the Cybersecurity Act 2; national designation in the meantime.
    Who acts
    Commission and co-legislators; CCB and sector regulators (CREG for energy) for designation.
    Success looks like
    Every platform that can switch more than the threshold is registered, supervised and uses two-step login.
    EU · NIS2 review / CSA2
  3. 53Stop fake bank calls and suspicious payments at the source
    For the average person · Voor de gewone burger

    Criminals call or text with the real number or name of your bank on the screen, and then talk you into moving your money. An 80-year-old cannot be expected to see through that. This idea puts the work where it can be done: phone companies block calls and messages that fake a bank's or the government's number, and banks hold back payments that show clear warning signs and share the loss if they ignore them.

    NL: Criminelen bellen of sms'en met het echte nummer of de naam van je bank op het scherm, en praten je dan je geld af. Van een 80-jarige kun je niet verwachten dat hij daar doorheen kijkt. Dit idee legt het werk waar het gedaan kan worden: telecombedrijven blokkeren oproepen en berichten die het nummer van een bank of van de overheid vervalsen, en banken houden betalingen met duidelijke alarmsignalen tegen en delen in het verlies als ze die negeren.

    What exactly
    Telecom operators block calls and text messages that falsely show the number or name of a bank or public service. Banks delay or stop payments that match known fraud patterns, warn the customer through a second channel, and share the loss when clear warning signs were ignored.
    Why (2026 evidence)
    Phishing losses in Belgium almost doubled, from €49 million to €93 million. Fake calls from "the bank" are the standard way pensioners lose their savings.
    Legal route
    The Payment Services Regulation now being finalised (liability for impersonation fraud, cooperation duty for telecom operators); Belgian telecom law for number blocking.
    Who acts
    Co-legislators; BIPT and telecom operators; banks and Febelfin; the National Bank as supervisor.
    Success looks like
    Faked bank numbers no longer reach Belgian phones; fraud losses fall year on year.
    EU / BE · PSR

VPNA protected, private connection over the internet.Een beveiligde, private verbinding over het internet.

NIS2The EU law that obliges important organisations (hospitals, energy, transport…) to secure their systems and report serious attacks.De Europese wet die belangrijke organisaties (ziekenhuizen, energie, vervoer…) verplicht hun systemen te beveiligen en zware aanvallen te melden.

CyberFundamentals (CyFun)The CCB's free security checklist for organisations.De gratis veiligheidschecklist van het CCB voor organisaties.

PUK codeThe code that unlocks a SIM card; with it a criminal can take over a phone number.De code die een simkaart ontgrendelt; daarmee kan een crimineel een gsm-nummer overnemen.

Protect yourself · Bescherm jezelf
In plain words · In gewone woorden

Which of the 31 countries tell people to keep an emergency stock at home, what the advice contains, and what changed in 2025–2026. It is precaution, not a warning that an attack is coming.

NL: Welke van de 31 landen mensen vragen thuis een noodvoorraad te hebben, wat het advies inhoudt en wat er in 2025–2026 veranderde. Het is voorzorg, geen waarschuwing dat er een aanval komt.

Ready at home: what governments tell people to keep in stock

Of the 31 countries covered, 18 have official advice to keep an emergency stock at home (Confirmed: from the government or agency itself), 9 have it only through media reports (Reported) and 4 have none found in the sources checked. Where the advice gives a length, it is 72 hours (3 days) in 17 countries (some say "at least"), about one week in 4 (Estonia, Norway, Sweden and Switzerland) and 10 to 14 days in 1 (Austria); 5 give no single figure (Croatia, Ireland, Liechtenstein, Romania and Slovakia). This is precautionary advice, not a warning that an attack is coming.

NL: Van de 31 landen hebben 18 officieel advies om thuis een noodvoorraad te hebben (Bevestigd: van de overheid of het agentschap zelf), 9 enkel via mediaberichten (Gemeld) en 4 geen gevonden in de gecontroleerde bronnen. Waar het advies een duur noemt, is dat 72 uur (3 dagen) in 17 landen (soms "minstens"), ongeveer een week in 4 (Estland, Noorwegen, Zweden en Zwitserland) en 10 tot 14 dagen in 1 (Oostenrijk); 5 geven geen duidelijk cijfer (Kroatië, Ierland, Liechtenstein, Roemenië en Slowakije). Dit is voorzorgsadvies, geen waarschuwing dat er een aanval komt.

In plain words

What the advice is. Be able to cope at home, without outside help, for at least 72 hours (three days); some countries ask for a week or more. The lists usually name drinking water, food that keeps or needs no cooking, necessary medicines, a battery or wind-up radio, a torch and some cash (18 of the 27 lists with advice include cash).

Why it is in a file about cyberattacks. The authorities name long power cuts and outages of water and communications among the reasons, and some name cyberattacks directly. Luxembourg's government says its guide prepares households for a prolonged power cut, natural disaster or cyberattack. The guide of France's national defence and security secretariat (SGDSN) covers cyberattacks and armed conflict among its scenarios. The Icelandic booklet mentions power cuts, cyberattacks, technical failures and international tension. The European Commission lists extreme weather, power outages, cyber and hybrid threats and conflict. Other countries mainly cite storms, floods and blackouts, so not every guide mentions cyberattacks.

What is old and what is new. The idea is not new: in 10 countries the sources show a guide or campaign from before 2025 (for example Norway mailed households in 2018 and Latvia published its 72-hour booklet in 2020). What is new in 2025–2026 is formal campaigns and household mailings, listed below.

Precaution, not a warning. Several authorities said so explicitly. Belgium's National Crisis Centre stresses that it does not want to cause panic (VRT NWS). According to media, Iceland's Justice Minister said the booklet is not a response to a specific threat. Croatia's Interior Ministry said the push is not tied to a specific expected event. Cyprus's Civil Defence deputy spokesperson said the EU recommendation should not be read as a warning that war is imminent. The acting director of Slovenia's civil protection administration said the aim is to prepare for unpredictable events, not to frighten.

Wat het advies is. Thuis minstens 72 uur (drie dagen) zonder hulp van buitenaf kunnen overleven; sommige landen vragen een week of meer. De lijsten noemen meestal drinkwater, voeding die houdbaar is of niet gekookt hoeft te worden, noodzakelijke medicijnen, een radio op batterijen of krachtstroom, een zaklamp en wat contant geld (18 van de 27 lijsten met advies bevatten contant geld).

Waarom dit in een dossier over cyberaanvallen staat. De autoriteiten noemen langdurige stroomuitval en storingen van water en communicatie als redenen, en sommige noemen cyberaanvallen rechtstreeks. De regering van Luxemburg zegt dat haar gids huishoudens voorbereidt op een langdurige stroomuitval, natuurramp of cyberaanval. De gids van het Franse nationale secretariaat voor defensie en veiligheid (SGDSN) behandelt onder meer cyberaanvallen en gewapend conflict. Het IJslandse boekje noemt stroomuitval, cyberaanvallen, technische storingen en internationale spanning. De Europese Commissie noemt extreem weer, stroomuitval, cyber- en hybride dreigingen en conflict. Andere landen noemen vooral stormen, overstromingen en black-outs, dus niet elke gids vermeldt cyberaanvallen.

Wat oud is en wat nieuw. Het idee is niet nieuw: in 10 landen tonen de bronnen een gids of campagne van vóór 2025 (Noorwegen stuurde bijvoorbeeld al in 2018 een brochure naar de huishoudens en Letland publiceerde zijn 72-urenboekje in 2020). Nieuw in 2025–2026 zijn formele campagnes en bedelingen aan huishoudens, hieronder opgelijst.

Voorzorg, geen waarschuwing. Meerdere autoriteiten zeiden dat uitdrukkelijk. Het Belgische Nationaal Crisiscentrum benadrukt dat het geen paniek wil zaaien (VRT NWS). Volgens media zei de IJslandse minister van Justitie dat het boekje geen reactie is op een specifieke dreiging. Het Kroatische ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken zei dat de oproep niet aan een specifiek verwacht evenement is gekoppeld. De woordvoerder van de Cypriotische civiele bescherming zei dat de EU-aanbeveling niet gelezen moet worden als een waarschuwing dat oorlog op handen is. De waarnemend directeur van de Sloveense civiele bescherming zei dat het erom gaat voor onvoorspelbare gebeurtenissen klaar te zijn, niet om bang te maken.

Belgium

Belgium ConfirmedThe National Crisis Centre (NCCN) advises a 72-hour emergency kit. Campaign "Samen voorbereid" launched 21 April 2026, planned to run four years.
Official advice
Yes Confirmed
Agency
Nationaal Crisiscentrum / Centre de crise national (NCCN), federal
Guide or campaign
Campaign 'Samen voorbereid' / 'Prêts ensemble' (four years) with the brochure 'Samen voorbereid' and the page 'Een noodpakket bij je thuis'
First
21 April 2026 (campaign launch, per VRT); brochure news item around 1 October 2026
Latest
Brochure launch reported 1 October 2026 (VRT); campaign planned to run four years
How long
72 hours
What to keep
A 72-hour emergency kit: water and food for at least 3 days (long-life, no cooking needed), necessary medicines for at least 72 hours, torch, battery or wind-up radio, power bank, hygiene items, basic first-aid kit, a small amount of cash, pet food. The NCCN distinguishes a compact evacuation backpack from a larger kit kept at home, and says no expensive pre-packed kit is needed.
Water
3 to 10 litres per person per day (as reported from the Crisiscentrum page; not checked against the page itself)
Sent to every household?
Public campaign online and in media; brochure available online (NL/FR/DE/EN) and a print-ready version offered to authorities and organisations. A mailing to every household was not found in the sources checked.
Why the authorities give it
The NCCN says emergencies can happen 'anywhere and at any time' and stresses that it does not want to cause panic; it wants people to be able to cope alone in the first 72 hours, when help may take time (per VRT NWS). One secondary source links the campaign to geopolitical tension and climate change; the NCCN itself naming war was not found in the sources checked.
What changed in 2025–2026
21 April 2026: Crisiscentrum launched the four-year 'Samen voorbereid' campaign recommending a 72-hour kit (VRT NWS, Business AM, Paris Match). About 1 October 2026: brochure 'Samen voorbereid' published (VRT, Crisiscentrum newsroom). Regional governments (Brussels, Flanders, Wallonia): no separate regional kit advice found; the municipality of Jette republished the federal campaign.

What the sources say

The federal National Crisis Centre (NCCN) launched the four-year campaign 'Samen voorbereid' on 21 April 2026. It advises a 72-hour emergency kit with water, food that needs no cooking, medicines, a torch and a radio, and distinguishes a compact evacuation backpack from a larger kit kept at home. According to VRT NWS (21 April 2026), no expensive pre-packed kit is needed, and the centre stresses that it does not want to cause panic. A mailing to every household was not found in the sources checked. Details are taken from the NCCN brochure and pages and from VRT NWS.

NL: Het federale Nationaal Crisiscentrum (NCCN) lanceerde op 21 april 2026 de vierjarige campagne 'Samen voorbereid'. Het raadt een noodpakket voor 72 uur aan, met water, voeding die niet gekookt hoeft te worden, medicijnen, een zaklamp en een radio, en maakt onderscheid tussen een compacte evacuatierugzak en een groter pakket thuis. Volgens VRT NWS (21 april 2026) is er geen duur kant-en-klaar pakket nodig, en benadrukt het centrum dat het geen paniek wil zaaien. Een bedeling aan elk huishouden is in de gecontroleerde bronnen niet gevonden. De details komen uit de brochure en de pagina's van het NCCN en uit VRT NWS.
