The first prison sentences in Europe for cutting sea cables.Confirmed
26 Jan 2026
Cables		Latvia–Gotland again. A fibre cable failed; NATO and police investigated. No outcome found.Reported
Jan 2026
Response		Thirteen countries and Iceland speak together. A joint statement on growing interference with satellite navigation for shipping in the Baltic and the North Sea.Confirmed
2024–2026
Signals		Jamming becomes normal. Flights meeting satellite-navigation interference rose from about 200 a day in early 2024 to about 900 a day by the second quarter, on a secondary count. Lithuania says transmitters in Kaliningrad can falsify signals up to 450 km away, which covers much of Poland, the Baltic states and part of the Nordic countries.Reported Claimed
3 Jul 2026
Signals		The air safety agency raises the alarm again. EASA issued the fourth revision of its safety bulletin on satellite-navigation outages, saying incidents are becoming more severe, more sophisticated and more disruptive. Its worst-affected list for mid-July 2026 included Tallinn, Riga, Helsinki, Vilnius and Warsaw, alongside Ankara and Istanbul.Confirmed
Oct 2026
Signals		It reaches space. A Danish technical university study found that the jamming over Europe also disturbs the position-finding of satellites in low orbit as they pass over.Confirmed
9 Nov 2026
Signals		The North Sea. About 80 aircraft over north-west Europe, including planes approaching Amsterdam, lost or lost confidence in their satellite position. Seven of them had navigation trouble on approach to Schiphol. Dutch air traffic control calls deliberate jamming a plausible explanation and says safety was not compromised; the Dutch investigation is still open and no official finding exists. A data analyst places the source 80 to 110 nautical miles north of Texel, where six Russian-flagged ships were sailing; shipping news sites say three of them are on the EU sanctions list for carrying weapons. Belgium’s own air traffic service told VRT it received no reports of jamming or spoofing that day. The disturbance is confirmed; who caused it is suspected, and the Belgian part is weaker than first reported.Confirmed Suspected

How many cables, and how sure anyone is

CountWho counts it that way
7 cuts between November 2024 and January 2025One tally of the intense period
At least 11 cables damaged since late 2023, plus a gas pipelineA wider tally including the earlier cases
None since January 2025One research institute, writing in 2026. It contradicts the Fitburg case of 31 December 2025 and the Latvian cable of January 2026, both in this table.
1 case proven in courtFitburg, Helsinki, November 2026
1 case proven not to be sabotageVezhen, Swedish prosecutors, 2025

The disagreement is not sloppiness: it is what happens when a count depends on whether you include accidents, pipelines, repeat damage to one cable, and incidents outside the Baltic.

Why these two are different from everything else in this file

  • No computer is involved. A cable is cut by an anchor and a signal is drowned out by a transmitter. None of the cyber laws in this file, and none of the two-step logins, make any difference.
  • Nobody owns the problem. Cables are laid by private companies in international water. Satellite navigation is run from space by other states. The affected country often has no jurisdiction over any part of it.
  • Deniability is built in. A dragging anchor looks like bad seamanship, which is why the Vezhen case matters: it proved that sometimes it really is.
  • The damage is invisible until it is total. Jamming hurt nobody for two years. Ships and aircraft carry other instruments and crews are trained. But it is now routine, and the experts quoted say the real danger is not jamming but spoofing, where false positions are fed in and believed.

Proven and not proven

ProvenNot proven
Two men were convicted of cutting cables in the Baltic, in November 2026.That anyone ordered them to. The verdict names no state.
One widely reported "sabotage" was weather and poor seamanship.How many of the others were accidents too.
Satellite-navigation interference is severe, widespread and increasing, on the air safety agency’s own assessment.Who is responsible for any single event, including 9 November 2026.
Jamming now disturbs satellites in orbit as well as aircraft.That it has caused any accident: no case found.
NATO patrols the Baltic for this.Whether the patrol is why incidents fell: the claim is relayed at second hand.

What it shows: This is the part of the picture where Europe reacted fastest and most physically: warships in the Baltic within weeks, a joint statement by fourteen coastal states, prison sentences inside a year. It is also the part where the country suffering the damage can do least on its own. For Belgium the lesson is narrow and practical: it has no Baltic, but it has the North Sea, the cables that come ashore there, and an airport that was already stopped twice by things in the sky. The signal that failed over the North Sea on 9 November 2026 is the first time this reached Belgium’s own doorstep.NL – Wat het toont: Dit is het deel van het beeld waar Europa het snelst en het meest fysiek reageerde: oorlogsschepen in de Oostzee binnen enkele weken, een gezamenlijke verklaring van veertien kustlanden, gevangenisstraffen binnen het jaar. Het is ook het deel waar het getroffen land zelf het minst kan doen. Voor België is de les smal en praktisch: het heeft geen Oostzee, maar wel de Noordzee, de kabels die daar aan land komen, en een luchthaven die al twee keer is stilgelegd door iets in de lucht. Het signaal dat op 9 november 2026 uitviel boven de Noordzee is de eerste keer dat dit voor de Belgische deur kwam.

Still open

  • Who caused the loss of satellite positioning over the North Sea on 9 November 2026.
  • Whether anyone ordered the Fitburg crew to drag their anchor.
  • What happened to the investigations into the February 2025 and January 2026 cable failures.
  • Whether the NATO patrol actually reduced the incidents, from a primary source.
  • An agreed count of damaged cables: every tally differs.
  • Whether the cables coming ashore in Belgium are watched at all: nothing found.

PUK codeThe code that unlocks a SIM card; with it a criminal can take over a phone number.De code die een simkaart ontgrendelt; daarmee kan een crimineel een gsm-nummer overnemen.
sandbox / test environmentA closed-off space where software or AI is tested without access to the real world.Een afgesloten ruimte waarin software of AI getest wordt zonder toegang tot de echte wereld.
frontier AIThe most powerful, newest AI systems.De krachtigste, nieuwste AI-systemen.
MythosAn Anthropic AI model that is very good at finding holes in software.Een AI-model van Anthropic dat heel goed is in het vinden van lekken in software.
hacktivistA hacker who attacks for a political cause.Een hacker die aanvalt voor een politieke zaak.
NoName057(16)A pro-Russian hacker group that knocks websites offline.Een pro-Russische hackersgroep die websites platlegt.
wiperMalicious software that destroys data instead of stealing it.Kwaadaardige software die gegevens vernietigt in plaats van ze te stelen.
leak siteA criminal website where stolen data is published to pressure victims.Een criminele website waar gestolen gegevens gepubliceerd worden om slachtoffers onder druk te zetten.
attributionOfficially naming who carried out an attack.Officieel aanwijzen wie een aanval uitvoerde.
CyberFundamentals (CyFun)The CCB's free security checklist for organisations.De gratis veiligheidschecklist van het CCB voor organisaties.
SafeonwebThe CCB's warning and advice service for citizens and companies.De waarschuwings- en adviesdienst van het CCB voor burgers en bedrijven.
security operations centreA team that watches systems 24/7 to spot attacks early.Een team dat systemen 24 op 24 bewaakt om aanvallen vroeg te zien.
software bill of materialsThe ingredient list of a piece of software.De ingrediëntenlijst van een stuk software.
threat-led penetration testA test in which ethical hackers attack a bank as real criminals would.Een test waarbij ethische hackers een bank aanvallen zoals echte criminelen dat zouden doen.
CLOUD ActA US law that lets US authorities demand data from American companies, even data stored abroad.Een Amerikaanse wet waarmee Amerikaanse diensten gegevens kunnen opeisen bij Amerikaanse bedrijven, ook gegevens in het buitenland.
cloudComputer services and storage rented over the internet from a provider.Computerdiensten en opslag die je via het internet huurt bij een leverancier.
encryptionLocking data with a digital key so only the right person can read it.Gegevens vergrendelen met een digitale sleutel zodat alleen de juiste persoon ze kan lezen.
quantum computerA future, extremely powerful type of computer that could break today's encryption.Een toekomstig, extreem krachtig soort computer dat de versleuteling van vandaag kan kraken.
FPSFederal Public Service, a federal ministry (FOD/SPF).Federale Overheidsdienst, een federaal ministerie (FOD/SPF).
FPS BOSAThe federal ministry for policy and support, including government IT.De federale overheidsdienst Beleid en Ondersteuning, ook voor overheids-IT.
FAGGThe federal agency for medicines and health products.Het federaal agentschap voor geneesmiddelen en gezondheidsproducten.
BIPTThe Belgian telecom regulator.De Belgische telecomregulator.
SHIELDA Belgian platform where hospitals share cybersecurity services and knowledge.Een Belgisch platform waar ziekenhuizen cyberveiligheidsdiensten en kennis delen.
Audit VlaanderenThe Flemish audit body that checks local governments, including their IT security.De Vlaamse auditdienst die lokale besturen controleert, ook hun IT-veiligheid.
VVSG / UVCW / BrulocalisThe associations of Flemish, Walloon and Brussels municipalities.De verenigingen van Vlaamse, Waalse en Brusselse gemeenten.
OCMW / CPASThe local public social welfare centre.Het openbaar centrum voor maatschappelijk welzijn van de gemeente.
Card StopThe Belgian number to block bank cards: 078 170 170.Het Belgische nummer om bankkaarten te blokkeren: 078 170 170.
itsmeThe Belgian app for digital identification and signing.De Belgische app voor digitale identificatie en ondertekening.
MyMinfinThe federal tax administration's online portal.Het online portaal van de federale belastingadministratie.
EuroclearA Brussels financial company that holds most of the frozen Russian state assets.Een Brussels financieel bedrijf dat het grootste deel van de bevroren Russische staatstegoeden bewaart.
IRGCIran's Revolutionary Guards, a military force under Iran's supreme leader.De Iraanse Revolutionaire Garde, een militaire macht onder de opperste leider van Iran.
FSBRussia's domestic intelligence and security service.De Russische binnenlandse inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdienst.
State Security (VSSE)Belgium's civilian intelligence service.De Belgische burgerlijke inlichtingendienst (Staatsveiligheid).
Cyber ForceThe cyber branch of the Belgian armed forces.De cybercomponent van het Belgische leger.
Ivanti EPMMSoftware that organisations use to manage their staff's phones; its holes were used in several 2026 attacks.Software waarmee organisaties de gsm's van hun personeel beheren; de lekken erin werden in 2026 bij meerdere aanvallen gebruikt.
Fortinet / FortiBleedA firewall maker; 'FortiBleed' is the 2026 case in which its firewalls were hacked at scale.Een maker van firewalls; 'FortiBleed' is de zaak uit 2026 waarin zijn firewalls op grote schaal gehackt werden.
Reference · Naslag

Sources

Every source used in this file, 870 in all, sorted by type of source. Sources added for the pages on drones, sabotage and water carry a label saying which page they support.

In plain words

How to weigh them: an official statement or a court verdict is the strongest. A public broadcaster or news agency reporting what an authority said comes next. Trade press and security companies are useful for technical detail but can have a commercial interest. Research counts depend on the definitions the researchers chose. Reference works such as Wikipedia are used only to find the original report, never as proof.

NL: Hoe je ze weegt: een officiële verklaring of een vonnis is het sterkst. Daarna komt een openbare omroep of persagentschap dat meldt wat een overheid zei. Vakpers en beveiligingsbedrijven zijn nuttig voor technische details, maar kunnen een commercieel belang hebben. Tellingen van onderzoekers hangen af van de definities die ze kozen. Naslagwerken zoals Wikipedia dienen alleen om het oorspronkelijke bericht te vinden, nooit als bewijs.

How they were checked. Sources were found through web searches (10–12 November 2026 for the cyber pages, 13–15 November 2026 for drones, sabotage and water). For the pages added on 13–15 November the facts were taken from the search results for each link; the linked pages were not opened one by one, because direct page access is blocked in the working environment. Facts resting on a single report are marked "Reported" on the page itself.

In plain words · In gewone woorden

An index of every subject in this file, the subjects still to come, and the questions public sources do not answer.

NL: Een index van elk onderwerp in dit dossier, de onderwerpen die nog komen, en de vragen die publieke bronnen niet beantwoorden.

Subjects in this file, and what is still open

An index of the subjects worked out in this file, the subjects still to come, and the questions that public sources do not answer.

In plain words

This file started as a register of cyberattacks. It now also covers things that are not hacks at all: drones, arson, cut cables, fake videos. Each subject is done twice, first for Belgium and then for the other 30 countries, and each line carries a label saying how firm the fact is. This page is the way in, and the honest list of what is still missing.

NL: Dit dossier begon als een register van cyberaanvallen. Het behandelt nu ook zaken die helemaal geen hacks zijn: drones, brandstichting, doorgesneden kabels, nepvideo’s. Elk onderwerp is twee keer gedaan, eerst voor België en dan voor de andere 30 landen, en elke regel draagt een label dat zegt hoe hard het feit is. Deze pagina is de ingang, en de eerlijke lijst van wat nog ontbreekt.

What is next

SubjectWhat it would cover
Encryption and "chat control"What the stalled EU child-protection regulation would require of messaging apps, the security argument against weakening encryption, and where each country stands.
Skills and jobsThe size of the shortage per country and per sector, what retraining exists, and how military cyber reserves are recruited.

What is still open

The questions below are the ones that public sources did not answer by 21 November 2026. Each is repeated under "Still open" on the page it belongs to.

WhereThe question
Who did itFor most incidents nobody is named, and for the big hacks the proof stops at a government statement whose evidence stays secret.
Belgium, the freezer attacksOne minister points at Iran, the foreign minister and the federal prosecutor do not confirm. No Belgian attribution exists.
Belgium, the drones of 2025The federal prosecutor’s investigations into the sightings have produced nothing public, and the air security centre’s status is unclear.
Belgium, hospitalsHow many reached the legal cybersecurity level by the deadline of 18 April 2026 is not published.
Belgium, waterWhether any Belgian water company has looked for control devices reachable from the internet, and what it found.
Belgium, defenceThe size of the Cyber Force, and whether its rapid teams have ever been sent to help a hospital or a town hall.
EuropeWho sent the hoax bomb threats of November 2026, and what caused the loss of satellite positioning over the North Sea on 9 November 2026.

What it shows: The gaps are not random. They sit almost always at the same place: between an event everyone can see, and the name of whoever caused it. That is why this file keeps the two apart on every page.NL – Wat het toont: De gaten zijn niet toevallig. Ze zitten bijna altijd op dezelfde plek: tussen een gebeurtenis die iedereen kan zien, en de naam van wie ze veroorzaakte. Daarom houdt dit dossier die twee op elke pagina uit elkaar.
